body:
I think the example is outdated. Looking at the source code (latest ai-sdk/anthropic 2.0.23),
- `citations` is not part of `AnthropicProviderOptions`: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/92dadc07893b0525da8d08ab31930f55f0149611/packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-options.ts#L56-L84
- There is a `AnthropicFilePartProviderOptions` with `citations` in the same file. It is exported in the file but not exported in the [index.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/92dadc07893b0525da8d08ab31930f55f0149611/packages/anthropic/src/index.ts). Hence, I cannot import `AnthropicFilePartProviderOptions`.
  - Also, the source code mentions it should be used for document citations, no web search

Then, there is also this PR in draft about citations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5368

At least for me, the state of citations is also unclear. Based on the documentation (v5), the source code, this issue and the linked PR, I could not figure out how to use inline citations from Anthropic with setting provider options, especially when using inline citations with the [web search tool](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#citations).

The underlying Anthropic message contains the inline citation content such as `cited_text`. You can access with `streamText` on the backend by:
1. Setting `includeRawChunks` to `true`
2. Implementing an [onChunk](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/stream-text#on-chunk) handler that extract `TextStreamPart` of type `raw`.
3. Sending the data from backend to the frontend. Not sure what the best approach is here. You can send it as a custom data part but then you need to match the data part with the message part id manually?!

It would be nice if this citation information from the underlying anthropic message is passed to the `UIMessage` and its underlying parts, e.g. `TextUIPart.providerMetadata` so that it is available on the frontend, matching the same message part id. In other words, we should be able to use this feature with the [Inline Citation](https://ai-sdk.dev/elements/components/inline-citation) component from ai-elements.

More context that might help someone.

If you followed this [human in the loop](https://ai-sdk.dev/cookbook/next/human-in-the-loop) tutorial you may have unknowingly shot yourself in the foot. Because only the last message is evaluated for tool calling results if you send a message on top of a pending tool call you receive the error discussed here and your LLM never responds from here on out.

Disabling the user input while the last message is awaiting confirmation as the example suggests is likely not enough. To be safe you should check all past messages for non tool results either delete them or set a "skipped tool call" tool result.

body:
The underlying issue was a bug that message annotations were split between different assistant response messages. This bug was fixed by combining assistant messages into one. Also ideally UI message should be a sequence of user-assistant-user-assistant messages to make rendering in the UI easy, and combining assistant messages achieves that. Many users reporting that they needed to put hacks in place to combine assistant messages.

With this in mind, I have introduced `parts` on UI messages: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4670

Check out this example of using message parts with tool invocations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/next-openai/app/use-chat-tools/page.tsx

I hope message parts are the way forward here. Please let me know if that addresses the limitations that you were facing, and if there are missing features in the new approach.

Still not clear to me why structured outputs should be enabled by default as it is not the default behavior of the models. I'd propose to adhere to the default behavior of the model providers. Also we should consider that not all models and/or providers even support structured outputs.

Can you share more details on why the ai sdk plans to defer from the defaults of all model providers?

PS: structured outputs needs to be configured separately and is just useful for very specific use-cases, but not for the standard chat-completion, afaik.
author: hopkins385

body:
@hopkins385 contrast the 2 options:

1) structured outputs are opt-in: sometimes the model will return bad completions that cannot be parsed, leading to unforeseen errors in production
2) structured outputs are opt-out: you discover immediately when your schema is incompatible (provider error during dev time) and you can opt-out. by default, the model will always return correct completions, preventing parsing errors in production. you know when you opted out and created a risk

that's why i think opt-out is preferrable
author: lgrammel

body:
By having the opt-out option you are assuming everyone prefers to configure a JSON schema and parse the output of the llm. Which means the main use-case is not chat-completion. But afaik this is not the case as the main use-case is just forwarding the tokens to the client (e.g. chat scenario).

As openai writes in their docs:
"Structured Outputs is a feature that ensures the model will always generate responses that adhere to your supplied JSON Schema, so you don't need to worry about the model omitting a required key, or hallucinating an invalid enum value." [source](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs)

I think "features" should always be opt-in.

body:
Confirmed this remains open in the current AI SDK v7 canary source (`b4507d5069e69e1da50cac0607d71bac2f5ac495`, June 11, 2026): `generateImage()` still accepts no `telemetry` / `experimental_telemetry` option and does not dispatch through the registered telemetry integrations.

This is now a concrete coverage gap for OpenTelemetry-based observability integrations such as PostHog's `PostHogSpanProcessor`: text generations, embeddings, and reranking can be observed through the AI SDK telemetry lifecycle, but image generation requires application-specific manual spans. That also means image cost and provider errors cannot be captured plug-and-play.

PostHog's corresponding AI SDK v7 tracking issue is PostHog/posthog-js#3674. I avoided opening a duplicate AI SDK issue because this one describes the required core change directly.

body:
> I have introduced an `onError` callback on `streamText`: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4729 (`ai@4.1.22`)
> 
> `streamText` immediately starts streaming to enable sending data without waiting for the model.
> Errors become part of the stream and are not thrown to prevent e.g. servers from crashing.
> 
> To log errors, you can provide an `onError` callback that is triggered when an error occurs.
> 
> ```tsx highlight="6-8"
> import { streamText } from 'ai';
> 
> const result = streamText({
>   model: yourModel,
>   prompt: 'Invent a new holiday and describe its traditions.',
>   onError({ error }) {
>     console.error(error); // your error logging logic here
>   },
> });
> ```

That was fast. Thank you!

body:
Optimal DX in this case would be for `generateObject` to always accept a valid zod schema and transform based on the provider and their specs. If `oneOf` is not supported, it should not be included in the request as such, but as instructions instead (possibly as description, not sure how it's currently implemented for models that don't support structured outputs), and the error should be thrown only if the model generated a response that could not be validated against the schema (https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/ai-sdk-core/generating-structured-data#error-handling).

This approach is consistent with the ai sdks mission (https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/introduction#why-use-the-ai-sdk).

body:
The underlying issue was a bug that message annotations were split between different assistant response messages. This bug was fixed by combining assistant messages into one. Also ideally UI message should be a sequence of user-assistant-user-assistant messages to make rendering in the UI easy, and combining assistant messages achieves that. Many users reporting that they needed to put hacks in place to combine assistant messages.

With this in mind, I have introduced `parts` on UI messages: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4670

Check out this example of using message parts with tool invocations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/next-openai/app/use-chat-tools/page.tsx

I hope message parts are the way forward here. Please let me know if that addresses the limitations that you were facing, and if there are missing features in the new approach.

This relies on the assumption that reasoning is a single block followed by a text response, i.e. that the first text token marks the end of the reasoning process. While that's a reasonable assumption to make, the AI SDK currently allows for interleaved reasoning and text chunks, meaning that reasoning could resume after several text tokens have been sent.

For now it is probably best to use onChunk and send custom data. I'll think about how to best integrate it into the SDK.

body:
> The workaround is to use `ref` to force the component that hosts `useChat` to be recreated when it changes. Which is usually all the page. This is quite ugly but at least it works.

It is not only ugly, but won't work either. 

Consider this use case: user switches to another chat before the first one completes streaming, and then comes back to the first, and hit the stop button. 

If you force the component to rerender in order to respond to a reactive id, `useChat` will be called again, which will return a different `stop` function, which won't cancel the initial unfinished stream.

The current vue composable implementation is very largely **not** reactive, which makes it very difficult to work with. I think the API should be more native to vue instead of a mimic of the react one.

body:
The fix in #7246 helped but there's still a gap `pitstop-check` is catching:
```code
[WARN] packages/gateway/src/errors/gateway-rate-limit-error.ts:18 — 429 handled without Retry-After
[WARN] packages/provider/src/errors/api-call-error.ts:31 — CAP vs WAIT not distinguished
```
The retry layer now reads Retry-After (up to 60s), but the error types themselves don't expose the header value to callers implementing custom retry logic. So anyone wrapping the SDK — like the middleware example above — has to re-parse headers they've already seen.

The 60s cap is also the gap RickVM noted. Anthropic sometimes returns Retry-After: 600 for quota exhaustion. That's a STOP signal, not a WAIT signal — but the current logic treats it as exponential backoff.

Tool: https://github.com/SirBrenton/pitstop-check

Again, thank you all for helping us better identify this concern, which ties to a known, larger problem area with our `experimental_throttle` config option for `useChat`. Rather than ship a hacky patch fix (like the one in my PR above), we've decided to take time to explore a more robust solution in preparation for an upcoming major release.

In the meantime, you can reliably avoid the issue by:

1. Not using `experimental_throttle`
2. Explicitly adding delays before your usage of `addToolResult` / `onToolCall`!

For now, I'll be closing this issue and re-opening once we start/execute the more holistic solution!

I’ve been looking into this and started implementing the completion and structuredObject APIs in Angular. While doing so, I noticed an inconsistency between the documentation and the actual API behaviour:

According to the docs, passing an id to any of the three methods (chat, completion, structuredObject) should make them share state.

However, during v5 development, this shared state functionality was removed from the chat hook, but not from the completions or structuredObject hooks ([see commit](https://github.com/vercel/ai/commit/9ae327d7ba4176993769509b37c32369f186821d)).

I’m unsure if this is intentional. My understanding is that the goal is to let the application handle state sharing instead. If that’s the case, I think this behaviour should be consistent across all methods and the documentation updated accordingly.

IMHO, I think state sharing should be provided by the application code and not the framework and it will remove some complexity related to context management in the UI implementations.

body:
The underlying issue was a bug that message annotations were split between different assistant response messages. This bug was fixed by combining assistant messages into one. Also ideally UI message should be a sequence of user-assistant-user-assistant messages to make rendering in the UI easy, and combining assistant messages achieves that. Many users reporting that they needed to put hacks in place to combine assistant messages.

With this in mind, I have introduced `parts` on UI messages: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4670

Check out this example of using message parts with tool invocations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/next-openai/app/use-chat-tools/page.tsx

I hope message parts are the way forward here. Please let me know if that addresses the limitations that you were facing, and if there are missing features in the new approach.

body:
@lgrammel the OpenAI Agents SDK does this:
TLDR - automatically reset tool_choice to "auto" after a tool call

> To prevent infinite loops, the framework automatically resets tool_choice to "auto" after a tool call. This behavior is configurable via [agent.reset_tool_choice](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/ref/agent/#agents.agent.Agent.reset_tool_choice). The infinite loop is because tool results are sent to the LLM, which then generates another tool call because of tool_choice, ad infinitum.
> 
> If you want the Agent to completely stop after a tool call (rather than continuing with auto mode), you can set [Agent.tool_use_behavior="stop_on_first_tool"] which will directly use the tool output as the final response without further LLM processing.
> 

https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/agents/#forcing-tool-use

body:
Sorry for my late response.

If I understand correctly, after creating the openAICompatible provider, you can instantiate a certain model using the model identifier. Since every model has its own capabilities, it makes sense to allow for configuration of the model specifics. One of these specifics is if the model supports structuredObject output using a schema.

Currently, the openAiCompatible provider does not allow for providing these specifics.
Since the default for the configuration of the parameter `supportsStructuredOutputs` is `false` and there is no way in overriding this default config, the openAiCompatible provider will never add the given scheme to the requests on the LMStudio server. So, It seems to me that LMStudio is fully compatible with openai, but there is no way in configuring a given model to allow for structured output.

The PR to allow for this feature seems fairly easy:
- when creating a model from the provider, not just allow for the modelId and the settings, but also allow for model configuration
- merge this model configuration with the default configuration when creating the underlying `chatLanguageModel`, `completionModel` and `embeddingModel` models.

Shall I start this PR?
Do you have any guidelines available when contributing

author: ErikDakoda

body:
In conclusion, while it's possible to work through the other issues I mentioned by adjusting your schema, there is a bug concerning optional parameters. Both `type: ['string', 'null'],` in a JSON schema, and  `z.string().nullable()` in a Zod schema throw errors.

From OpenAi:

> Although all fields must be required (and the model will return a value for each parameter), it is possible to emulate an optional parameter by using a union type with null. Example:

```javascript
           "unit": {
                "type": ["string", "null"],
                "description": "The unit to return the temperature in",
                "enum": ["F", "C"]
            }
```

def check_genai_models():
    for model_id in [
        "gemini-2.5-pro",
        "gemini-2.5-flash",
        "gemini-2.0-flash-001",
        "gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001",
    ]:
        try:
            client = genai.Client(
                vertexai=True,
                project=PROJECT,
                location=LOCATION,
            )
            response: GenerateContentResponse = client.models.generate_content(
                model=model_id,
                contents="What's the largest planet in our solar system?",
                config=GenerateContentConfig(response_logprobs=True, logprobs=1),
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error with model {model_id}: {e}")
            continue
        else:
            print(f"Processing model: {model_id}")
            if response.candidates[0].avg_logprobs:
                avg_logprobs = response.candidates[0].avg_logprobs
                num_logprobs = len(response.candidates[0].logprobs_result.chosen_candidates)
                yield dict(
                    model=model_id,
                    logprobs=True,
                    avg_logprobs=avg_logprobs,
                    num_logprobs=num_logprobs,
                )
            else:
                yield dict(
                    model=model_id,
                    logprobs=False,
                    avg_logprobs=None,
                    num_logprobs=None,
                )


def main():
    results = pd.DataFrame.from_records(check_genai_models())
    print(results.head(10))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

I looked at your example route. It seems that your route doesn't use an abort signal on the streamText method: https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/advanced/stopping-streams

When I removed the abort signal from the streamText method, it correctly handles the error (as a side effect, it still completes the LLM call because it doesn't forward that abort signal which is why I had the abort signal there). body:
Following up, @brandonhays3 and @tunde-alao! 

While the PR above will address the network error caused by the unhandled abort error when using `abortSignal` + `consumeStream`, it doesn't actually address what I believe you're aiming to achieve: aborting the API call to the provider _and_ saving partial responses.

The intent of `consumeStream` is to allow the response to stream _fully_ and trigger the `onFinish` (if present); it _does not_ support invoking `onFinish` if the stream is cut short by an abort signal.

body:
Thank you! I did do that workaround (calling convertToCoreMessage on the UI messages first), and that did resolve my issue.

I'm a little concerned about resolving this with a documentation update for a couple of reasons:

1) The cacheControl pattern above is likely to be pretty frequent - it's the natural way to cache a large system prompt and then continue to append new user messages as a conversation progresses, which is the most common use case for Anthropic caching.
2) The failure case was very obscure - it look me the better part of a week to pin down what was happening, because the only thing that breaks is anthropic's caching, which doesn't cause any errors, and it only breaks when there are user messages with UI-specific parts appended (e.g. tool calling), so in my case it actually worked on the first turn of the conversation and then broke afterwards.

At the very least, the documentation on anthropic prompt caching (and any other message-level providerOptions - open AI image detail?) should probably be very explicit on this case in particular, since I don't think it would be clear to a user that passing in mixed message types could silently fail in this way.

body:
Some OpenAI-compatible providers use this field to pass non-image files, but the automatic MIME type detection overrides the user-provided type and mistakenly classifies them as images, leading to downstream issues.
It's recommended to prioritize the user-supplied mimeType and only fall back to detection when it's missing, to avoid misclassification and improve system predictability.

Was running into this issue on and off when experimenting with AI SDK v5 and using pnpm in a turborepo monorepo. I had some strange combination of:
- ai installed globally (new-ish verison)
- zod installed globally (old-ish version)
- ai and other sub-packages installed in several apps / packages in the monorepo (v5 alpha latest)
- zod installed in several apps / packages (latest)

When I dug inside one of the ai packages (specifically the @ai-sdk/provider-utils package) I saw that my machine was resolving the zod imports to my global, old-ish zod package and not the latest local version. Deleting the old global package installs resolved the issue for me!

body:
Do you mean like how I did it in the screenshot above? That's what I'm doing as well, but it isn't working unfortunately. It works for every case, except `"tool-result"`.

The reason it doesn't work is because of this definition:

```ts
type ToolResultUnion<TOOLS extends ToolSet> =
  ToToolResultObject<ToToolsWithDefinedExecute<ToToolsWithExecute<TOOLS>>>
```

Let's put in `ToolSet` for the `TOOLS` param:

- `ToToolsWithExecute<ToolSet>` (evaluates to) → `{}`
- `ToToolsWithDefinedExecute<{}>` → `{}`
- `ToToolResultObject<{}>` → `never` (*)

And therefore:

- `{ type: "tool-result" } & never` → `never`

And that's why "tool-result" is not part of the union of string literals above.

The issue is here (*). Ideally `ToToolResultObject<{}>` would return some generic `"tool-result"` structure, instead of `never`.

body:
Adding a paperclip-side data point in case it helps narrow this down: we hit the same `cacheCreationInputTokens=0 / cacheReadInputTokens=0` outcome **without** using `parts` — i.e. with plain `content: string` messages — when routing through the Vercel AI Gateway.

**Repro shape** (`src/lib/harness/loop.ts` in our codebase):

```ts
const result = await generateText({
  model: "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5", // routed via Vercel AI Gateway
  messages: [
    {
      role: "system",
      content: systemPromptString, // single string, no parts
      providerOptions: {
        anthropic: { cacheControl: { type: "ephemeral" } },
      },
    },
    { role: "user", content: userPromptString },
  ],
  tools,
  // …
});
```

System prompt is comfortably above the 2048-token Haiku threshold (XML-tagged role + tools list + binding docs).

**Versions:**
- `ai@6.0.168`
- `@ai-sdk/gateway@3.0.104`
- `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.71`

**Result, every turn:**
- `result.providerMetadata.anthropic.cacheCreationInputTokens` → `0`
- `result.providerMetadata.anthropic.cacheReadInputTokens` → `0`
- `inputTokens` grows turn-to-turn with no reuse, so caching is definitely not happening upstream.

We also tried `providerOptions.gateway.caching: "auto"` (the Gateway-level shorthand) — same result: `0/0` every turn.

**BYOK ruled out:** we previously had Anthropic BYOK on with depleted credit balance, which produced a double-attempt pattern in `providerMetadata.gateway.routing.modelAttempts[]`. We disabled BYOK in the Gateway dashboard so each call is now a single `credentialType: "system"` attempt — caching still 0/0. So the issue isn't BYOK routing.

So this seems wider than the `parts`-only case described in the original report — it also affects the canonical `content: string` + message-level `providerOptions` shape when routed through the Gateway.

Happy to share dumps of `result.providerMetadata` and full request/response if helpful — just let me know what would move the needle.

body:
I ran into a blocker.

The `maxImagesPerCall` getter is defined in `ImageModelV2`, it's currently implemented for 10 providers

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/9bd5ab57a32142e55654ee805134b609ef33f605/packages/openai/src/openai-image-model.ts#L26-L30

In the implementations, the getter always accesses `this.settings` which is set in the constructor. If we remove the `settings` constructor option, we need replace the `maxImagesPerCall` getter with a method that accepts an argument, either a number for `maxImagesPerCall` or the whole `providerOptions` object. 

For #6078 we need to make `maxImagesPerCall` async anyway, so turning it into a function would be an obvious step in preparation for that.

Also the value for `maxImagesPerCall` is accessed before calling `.doGenerate()`

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/9bd5ab57a32142e55654ee805134b609ef33f605/packages/ai/core/generate-image/generate-image.ts#L113-L142

So we cannot pass through `settings.maxImagesPerCall` through `.doGenerate({providerOptions})`. We need that information in order to calculate how often `doGenerate()` needs to be called.

~~I suggest we change the `.maxImagesPerCall` getter into `.getMaxImagesPerCall(providerOptions)`. Would that work~~

I suggest we add the check if `maxImagesPerCall` is set on `providerOptions[provider]` in the `generateImage()` method

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/136819b8f27d1e5fdc51a5bd2802aafc3782ba13/packages/ai/core/generate-image/generate-image.ts#L113-L115
author: gr2m

body:
> I suggest we change the `.maxImagesPerCall` getter into `.getMaxImagesPerCall(providerOptions)`. Would that work?

After discussing with @samdenty, I suggest we remove the `.maxImagesPerCall` getter altogether. The `generateImage()` in the `ai` package is currently the only place that accesses the getter and it already has a fallback to `1` implemented.

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/9bd5ab57a32142e55654ee805134b609ef33f605/packages/ai/core/generate-image/generate-image.ts#L113-L115

I suggest we update that line to something like

```js
  const maxImagesPerCall = providerOptions[modelName].maxImagesPerCall ?? 1;
```
author: gr2m

body:
Another thing that came up is that we currently pass provider options directly through to the API call:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/136819b8f27d1e5fdc51a5bd2802aafc3782ba13/packages/ai/core/generate-image/generate-image.ts#L138

But `maxImagesPerCall` is not an option that is meant to be passed to the API, the number of requested images is already passed as `n`. `maxImagesPerCall` is used to calculate how many requests need to be sent

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/136819b8f27d1e5fdc51a5bd2802aafc3782ba13/packages/ai/core/generate-image/generate-image.ts#L113-L142

For now I'll add logic to remove `maxImagesPerCall` from `providerOptions` before passing it to the `doGenerate()` method

body:
We discussed with @lgrammel.

The two challenges I'm facing

1. The `imageSettings` have been used before the `.doGenerate()` call, e.g. to retrieve `maxImagesPerCall` in order to calculate how many calls need to be done. We will address it by turning `maxImagesPerCall` into a method that retrieves the `providerOptions` as argument.
2. If we move `imageSettings` into `providerOptions`, they end up in the request body which we don't want. In order to address that, Lars suggested to take a look at the `parseProviderOptions()` method used by language models, e.g.
https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/3a961cbbea7176cf6415e209f589379a43bdc943/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-language-model.ts#L98-L102

I'll prepare another PR for a base of discussion. We plan on pairing on it on Wednesday
author: gr2m

body:
I suggest we do the following

1. Move `maxImagesPerCall` to a top level argument for `generateImage()`, because it's used by every image model.

   Before
 
   ```js
   await generateImage({
     model: openai.image("dall-e-2", { maxImagesPerCall: 5 }),
     prompt,
     n: 10,
   });
   ```
 
   After
 
   ```js
   await generateImage({
     model: openai.image("dall-e-2"),
     prompt,
     n: 10,
     maxImagesPerCall: 5
   });
   ```

2. Add a private method such as `providerOptionsToApiRequestOptions` that by default just passes through `providerOptions[providerName]`, but can be used to remove other options such as `pollIntervalMillis` and `maxPollAttempts` in [LumaImageSettings](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/6f231db12f5dc57e358f2be0d8948f2937460fb7/packages/luma/src/luma-image-settings.ts#L17-L29) and `user` in [OpenAICompatibleImageSettings](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/a6b55ccee1f8eb86136c6d500cc20fa4ae7d81c7/packages/openai-compatible/src/openai-compatible-image-settings.ts#L4-L8)

Let me know what you think.
author: gr2m

body: I ended up not implementing the `providerOptionsToApiRequestOptions` method because the `ImageModelV2` classes are not extending a generic `ImageModelV2` class, they just implement the `ImageModelV2` interface. We could add an `providerOptionsToApiRequestOptions` method to `ImageModelV2` and make it optional, then check if the method was implemented by the current `ImageModelV2` implementation before passing `providerOptions` through it. But given that only two `ImageModelV2` implementations are currently affected by it, I just left the current implementation which does the extraction manually [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/0bc15b8af223b2fe1a2a0fd9d4f296ce60c9e22b/packages/luma/src/luma-image-model.ts#L80-L81). It doesn't seem that the `user` key is used at all in the OpenAICompatibleImageModel ([source](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/v5-gr2m/6077-ImageModelV2-move-settings-to-providerOptions-and-maxImagesPerCall/packages/openai-compatible/src/openai-compatible-image-model.ts)).

body:
It probably is, but I was unable to proceed using the SDK because this bug happened every time in my use case.  I'm implementing an assistant in our app that has various "modes" that map to the tools available.  So if a user says "Create a jira ticket", the LLM will use the "switchMode" tool to switch into that mode, then follow up with a call to one of the new tools that I add.

The switchMode worked fine, but the follow up tool usage call ALWAYS fired twice, and it made it really hard to deal with the response.  onFinish would fire twice, and I had no way of knowing which message was real and which wasn't.  On top of that, I'm paying for 2x tokens which just feels dumb.

In the end, I implemented my own useChat variant that is simpler to use and doesn't auto submit the next call after adding all the tool results.   

I appreciate this is a fast moving space, and the backend part (generate/streamText) is great to work with, but the front end SDK feels a bit clunky and over complicated to me.  I'd prefer a simpler interface that does less stuff, for example, I'd prefer having addToolResult not auto submit, but let me do it some how.

body:
Right now, ArkType is not compatible with the `jsonSchema` helper provided by AI SDK. For example:

```typescript
import { type } from "arktype"
import { jsonSchema } from "ai'

const schema = jsonSchema(type({}).toJsonSchema())
```

Gives error:
```
Argument of type 'NonBooleanBranch' is not assignable to parameter of type 'JSONSchema7'.
  Type 'Constrainable' is not assignable to type 'JSONSchema7'.
    Types of property '$defs' are incompatible.
      Type 'Record<string, NonBooleanBranch> | undefined' is not assignable to type '{ [key: string]: JSONSchema7Definition; } | undefined'.
        Type 'Record<string, NonBooleanBranch>' is not assignable to type '{ [key: string]: JSONSchema7Definition; }'.
          'string' index signatures are incompatible.
            Type 'NonBooleanBranch' is not assignable to type 'JSONSchema7Definition'.
              Type 'Constrainable' is not assignable to type 'JSONSchema7Definition'.ts(2345)
```

Unless you use the type assertion `... as JSONSchema7`

Hard to say whether this is an issue with AI SDK's `JSONSchema7` definition being too restrictive or ArkType's `JSONSchema.NonBooleanBranch` being too permissive.

body:
Facing a similar issue, using gemini-flash-2.0 model.

Required inputSchema
```
inputSchema: z.array(
      z.object({
        title: z.string(),
        description: z.string(),
        link: z.string(),
        bannerUrl: z.string(),
        technologies: z.array(z.string()),
      })
    )
```

Getting input schema from LLM.
```
inputSchema: z.object({
      input: z.array(
        z.object({
          title: z.string(),
          description: z.string(),
          link: z.string(),
          bannerUrl: z.string(),
          technologies: z.array(z.string()),
        })
      ),
    })
```

LLM unnecessary adding `input` key and instead of Array returning Array wrapped inside Object.

As a workaround updated my inputSchema to the one which LLM is returning. 
Bigger/better model might give good result but don't want to use bigger model as my task is small.

I was about to create an issue for `prepareRequestBody` in v5 but I found this issue. I'm running into a problem where `prepareRequestBody` (and everything with the ChatStore and ChatTransport I think) is fixed on first render. What I'm trying to do is integrate surrounding state and context into the `prepareRequestBody` function. In v4 it was a callback which allowed `prepareRequestBody` to change on every render.

I've made a simple reproduction case:

* https://github.com/zhm/ai-sdk-test
* `pnpm dev`
* http://localhost:3000/prepare-request-body
* Click Increment a few times to increment the counter
* Enter any message and click submit
* It always submits the `counter` as the initial value `0`

body:
There is a larger issue here. The abort signal from client to server that aborts the request cannot carry any additional information. Therefore the server cannot know whether the abort signal it receives was from an intentional abort, from a client disconnect (lost internet connection), or from e.g. the user closing the tab.

To solve this we would need to have a channel to the server that allows transporting that information. Websockets are one option, having an separate endpoint is another.

The dedicated endpoint solution has it's own pitfalls and requires architectural changes:
* for each request create a unique request id
* have a separate persistent route that allows stopping the request via id (and invoke it from the client when you want to stop)
* the hard part: keep a reference on the server to the abort signal for the ongoing server - ai provider streaming and share that in a way that is accessible for the separate stop endpoint (in particular in a distributed scenario where the abort request could arrive in a different machine or even data center).

body:
### Identify issue type

**Identified type: Bug**  
Confidence: High

Rationale: The issue describes a concrete failure of current AI SDK behavior: stopping a resumable stream via `useChat().stop()` does not abort the ongoing stream as expected. Although comments discuss architectural solutions and examples, the core report is broken stop/abort behavior.

Evidence:
- Reporter says `useChat({ id }).stop()` previously worked but no longer stops streams when using `createResumableStream` / `experimental_resume`.
- Reporter states the stream continues once started, with no way to stop it, potentially leaving orphaned server-side streamText processes.
- Other users confirm `stop()` problems, including only working in `submitted` status and not during `streaming`.
- Maintainer explains the abort signal cannot distinguish intentional stop from disconnect/tab close and that additional server communication is needed for proper abort handling.

body:
Opened #13468 for this.

The root cause here was that both telemetry attribute selectors were passing `NaN`/`Infinity` straight through to OpenTelemetry. I added a shared sanitizer so non-finite numeric attributes get dropped before they reach span exporters, and covered both the core helper path and the OpenTelemetry integration with regression tests.
author: theamodhshetty

body:
### Identify issue type

**Identified type: Bug**  
Confidence: High

Rationale: The report describes broken existing telemetry behavior that produces invalid OTLP output and causes trace export failures, with a reproduction and expected behavior to omit or sanitize non-finite numbers.

Evidence:
- SDK telemetry emits token-count span attributes such as `ai.usage.promptTokens` and `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` with JavaScript `NaN` values.
- OTLP JSON serialization turns these into `doubleValue: null`, violating OTLP schema and causing collectors to reject trace batches with HTTP/2 400 / InvalidArgument.
- The issue includes a concrete reproduction using `streamObject` with telemetry enabled and shows debug output containing `ai.usage.promptTokens: NaN`.
- A later comment states the root cause was telemetry attribute selectors passing `NaN`/`Infinity` through to OpenTelemetry and mentions adding a sanitizer/regression tests.

body:
I checked this against current `main` (`19736ee`, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@3.0.0-canary.54`). The OpenAI-compatible chat stream path now appears to normalize OpenAI-style snake_case usage fields.

The current stream regression in `packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.test.ts` includes an SSE usage chunk with `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens`, then verifies the finish event contains normalized usage under `inputTokens` / `outputTokens` while preserving the raw usage payload.

Validation I ran locally:

```sh
cd packages/openai-compatible
pnpm exec vitest --config vitest.node.config.js --run src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.test.ts -t "should stream reasoning content before text deltas"
```

Result: `1 passed | 92 skipped`.

So this looks fixed on current `main` for the chat streaming path. If this still reproduces on the latest canary with Langdock, a current final SSE chunk showing the `usage` object would be useful to tell whether there is a remaining provider-specific shape that is not covered by the existing converter.

**Identified type: Bug**  
Confidence: High

Rationale: The issue describes a concrete incorrect runtime behavior in existing streamText usage normalization for an OpenAI-compatible provider, with expected versus actual output. Even though a later comment suggests it may now be fixed, the issue is still a bug report.

Evidence:
- Reporter says streamText() with OpenAI-compatible Langdock returns onFinish usage as { promptTokens: null, completionTokens: null, totalTokens: null } despite API response containing snake_case usage fields.
- Expected behavior is normalization to SDK TokenUsage fields; suggested fix is to map prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens to camelCase.

Until you answer, here are concise highlights, practical tips, and sample day plans.

Top sights (don’t miss)
- Eiffel Tower (book tickets for summit in advance if you want to go up)
- Louvre (see the Mona Lisa, but also expect crowds — reserve timed entry)
- Musée d’Orsay (impressionist masterpieces)
- Notre-Dame / Île de la Cité and Sainte-Chapelle (stained glass)
- Montmartre & Sacré‑Cœur (views, artists’ square)
- Arc de Triomphe & Champs‑Élysées
- Le Marais (historic streets, shops, cafés)
- Latin Quarter & Luxembourg Gardens
- Centre Pompidou (modern art + architecture)
- Musée Rodin (sculptures in a lovely garden)
- Père Lachaise cemetery (famous graves, atmospheric)
- Palace of Versailles (day trip — allow half to full day)

Neighborhoods & experiences worth exploring
- Saint‑Germain-des-Prés: cafés, bookshops, elegant streets
- Canal Saint‑Martin: relaxed cafés and people-watching
- Rue Cler / Marché Bastille: food markets for local produce and snacks
- Rooftop/observation: Tour Montparnasse, Printemps/Galeries Lafayette terrace
- Seine river cruise (especially at sunset)
- Evening: cabaret (Moulin Rouge or Lido) or a dinner in a bistro

Food & drink tips
- Try croissants, pain au chocolat, fresh baguette, cheese, charcuterie, confit de canard, steak frites, macarons, crêpes
- For a memorable meal, book at least one bistro or Michelin spot in advance
- Visit a marché (market) for fresh produce and local snacks

Practical tips
- Buy museum/landmark tickets online in advance to skip long queues
- Get a carnet of metro tickets or a multi‑day pass depending on length of stay
- Expect pickpockets in touristy areas — keep valuables secure
- Walk a lot — Paris is very walkable and many gems are found wandering
- Learn basic French phrases (bonjour, s’il vous plaît, merci) — locals appreciate it
- Best times: spring and fall for milder weather and fewer crowds; early morning for museums

Sample itineraries
- 1 day (first‑time quick hit): Morning at Louvre → walk through Tuileries to Place de la Concorde → Champs‑Élysées to Arc de Triomphe → late afternoon/early evening at Eiffel Tower → Seine cruise at dusk.
- 3 days: Day 1 as above; Day 2 Musée d’Orsay + Latin Quarter + Sainte‑Chapelle + Notre‑Dame + Île Saint‑Louis; Day 3 Montmartre & Sacré‑Cœur + Le Marais + Centre Pompidou or shopping.
- 5 days: 3‑day plan + Day 4 Versailles day trip; Day 5 Père Lachaise, Canal Saint‑Martin, and relaxed café time or museum(s) you missed.

If you tell me your trip length and interests (art, food, shopping, kids, mobility constraints), I’ll make a tailored itinerary and include ticket suggestions and off‑the‑beaten‑path spots."}

A few quick questions that will help me tailor recommendations: how many days will you be there, and what do you like (museums, food, architecture, shopping, nightlife, walks, day trips)?

Meanwhile, here’s a compact, practical guide to the highlights and how to organize them.

Top must-sees
- Eiffel Tower — view from Champ de Mars or Trocadéro; book summit/second-floor tickets in advance or just enjoy the view from below at night when it’s lit and sparkling.  
- Louvre — world’s largest art museum (Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo); reserve timed-entry tickets.  
- Notre‑Dame area & Île de la Cité — the cathedral is under restoration (limited interior access), but Sainte‑Chapelle is an absolute jewel with its stained glass.  
- Montmartre & Sacré‑Cœur — hilltop basilica, artists’ square (Place du Tertre), great city views and winding streets.  
- Musée d’Orsay — Impressionists and post‑Impressionists in a former railway station.  
- Arc de Triomphe & Champs‑Élysées — climb the Arc for a great view down the grand avenue.  
- Le Marais — historic neighborhood, boutiques, cafés, Place des Vosges, and the Musée Carnavalet.  
- Centre Pompidou — modern art and an interesting rooftop panorama.

Museums & art (other top picks)
- Musée Rodin (sculpture & pretty gardens)  
- Musée de l’Orangerie (Monet’s Water Lilies)  
- Musée Picasso  
- Fondation Louis Vuitton (contemporary art & architecture)  
- Palais Galliera (fashion museum, check exhibitions)  

Neighborhoods & atmospheres
- Latin Quarter / Saint‑Germain — narrow streets, cafés, bookstores (Shakespeare & Co.), lively evening scene.  
- Canal Saint‑Martin — trendy cafés, picnic vibes, good for a relaxed walk.  
- Belleville — street art and local vibe.  
- Le Marais — great for Jewish and LGBTQ+ culture, small museums, shops.

Views & walks
- Seine river cruise (Bateaux Mouches) — lovely at sunset.  
- Rooftops: Tour Montparnasse observation deck (less crowded than Eiffel), many hotels and bars have rooftop terraces.  
- Luxembourg Gardens and Tuileries — great for relaxing and people-watching.

Food & markets
- Try bakery classics: croissant, pain au chocolat, baguette.  
- Pâtisseries: macarons (Ladurée, Pierre Hermé), tarte Tatin.  
- Bistros and brasseries — book for dinner in popular spots.  
- Food markets: Marché d’Aligre, Marché Bastille (Sundays/Thursdays) or Marché des Enfants Rouges (oldest covered market).  
- Wine bars, from casual to sommelier-led tastings.

Practical tips
- Buy tickets online for Eiffel, Louvre, and popular exhibitions to avoid long lines.  
- Metro is the fastest way to get around; buy a carnet (10 single tickets) or a short-term pass. Apps: Citymapper or RATP.  
- Museum opening closures: many museums close one weekday (Louvre closed Tue, Musée d’Orsay closed Mon — check current schedules).  
- Consider the Paris Museum Pass if you’ll visit multiple museums/monuments.  
- Be aware of pickpockets in crowded areas (metro, tourist sites).  
- Tipping: service is included, but leaving small change for good service is common.  
- Best seasons: spring and early autumn are ideal; summers are busy and can be hot.

Day trips (easy from Paris)
- Palace of Versailles — gardens and the Hall of Mirrors (allow a full day).  
- Giverny — Monet’s garden (spring–autumn).  
- Reims/Champagne region — tasting and cathedral tours.  
- Loire Valley châteaux (long day or overnight).  
- Disneyland Paris (if you travel with family).

Sample quick itineraries
- 1 day: Eiffel/Trocadéro → Seine cruise or walk → Louvre (or Musée d’Orsay) → Île de la Cité & Sainte‑Chapelle → dinner in Latin Quarter.  
- 3 days: Day 1: Louvre + Île de la Cité + Latin Quarter; Day 2: Eiffel + Trocadéro + Champs‑Élysées + Arc de Triomphe; Day 3: Montmartre + Musée d’Orsay or Le Marais + evening Seine cruise.  
- 5+ days: add Versailles, Giverny or a Loire/Champagne day trip and more neighborhood exploration.

author: gr2m

body:
It looks like the Vercel AI SDK may be filtering out the properties field when constructing the request body for Vertex AI. This could be due to an internal misinterpretation of [parameters.properties](https://parameters.properties/) versus object-level properties in the JSON schema.

Here are a few things you can try to debug and potentially resolve the issue:

Manually Inspect the SDK's Request ConstructionIf possible, log the raw request body before it's sent to Vertex AI and compare it with the expected schema. This could help pinpoint where properties is being dropped.

Force Inclusion of properties FieldYou might try explicitly wrapping properties in another object or giving it a unique key name (e.g., _properties) to see if that prevents filtering.

Check for Reserved Keywords HandlingSome SDKs internally reserve specific field names like properties. Check the documentation or source code of @ai-sdk/google-vertex for any such handling.

Validate Behavior Across Different VersionsIf possible, downgrade or upgrade @ai-sdk/google-vertex to see if the issue persists across versions.

Submit an Issue to Vercel AI SDK RepoIf this appears to be an SDK bug, consider reporting it in the repository. Provide a minimal reproduction case highlighting that the required field is being omitted.

Let me know if you need help testing this further! Given your methodical approach to problem-solving, I'm sure you'll uncover a workaround soon.

# Vercel AI SDK to OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions Mapping

This document provides a mapping from Vercel AI SDK telemetry attributes to the corresponding OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for generative AI operations.

## References

- [OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/gen-ai/)
- [Vercel AI SDK Telemetry Documentation](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/telemetry)

## Attribute Mappings

| **Vercel AI SDK Attribute**                | **OpenTelemetry Attribute**      | **Notes**                                                     | **Status**                |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `ai.model.id`                              | `gen_ai.request.model`           | Model name should be the exact model requested                | ✅ Already mapped in code |
| `ai.model.provider`                        | `gen_ai.system`                  | Provider/system name (e.g., `openai`, `anthropic`)            | ✅ Already mapped in code |
| `ai.usage.completionTokens`                | `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`     | Number of tokens in the completion/response                   | ✅ Already mapped in code |
| `ai.usage.promptTokens`                    | `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`      | Number of tokens in the prompt/input                          | ✅ Already mapped in code |
| `ai.prompt`                                | `gen_ai.prompt`                  | **DEPRECATED** - Use Event API to report prompt contents      | ⚠️ Deprecated             |
| `ai.response.text`                         | N/A                              | **DEPRECATED** - Use Event API to report completion contents  | ⚠️ Deprecated             |
| `ai.response.model`                        | `gen_ai.response.model`          | Actual model used for the response                            | 🔄 Needs mapping          |
| `ai.response.id`                           | `gen_ai.response.id`             | Unique identifier for the completion                          | 🔄 Needs mapping          |
| `ai.response.finishReason`                 | `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` | Reason(s) why generation finished (array format)              | 🔄 Needs mapping          |
| `ai.settings.maxRetries`                   | N/A                              | No direct OTEL equivalent                                     | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.request.headers.*`                     | N/A                              | No direct OTEL equivalent for request headers                 | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.telemetry.functionId`                  | N/A                              | Used for span naming, no direct OTEL equivalent               | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.telemetry.metadata.*`                  | N/A                              | Custom metadata, no direct OTEL equivalent                    | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.toolCall.name`                         | `gen_ai.tool.name`               | Name of the tool being called                                 | 🔄 Needs mapping          |
| `ai.toolCall.id`                           | `gen_ai.tool.call.id`            | Tool call identifier                                          | 🔄 Needs mapping          |
| `ai.toolCall.args`                         | N/A                              | Tool parameters - no direct OTEL equivalent                   | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.toolCall.result`                       | N/A                              | Tool result - no direct OTEL equivalent                       | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.usage.tokens`                          | `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`      | For embedding operations (input tokens)                       | 🔄 Needs mapping          |
| `ai.values`                                | N/A                              | Embedding input values - no direct OTEL equivalent            | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.embeddings`                            | N/A                              | Embedding output values - no direct OTEL equivalent           | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.response.timestamp`                    | N/A                              | No direct OTEL equivalent                                     | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.prompt.format`                         | N/A                              | No direct OTEL equivalent                                     | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.prompt.messages`                       | N/A                              | **DEPRECATED** - Use Event API to report messages             | ⚠️ Deprecated             |
| `ai.prompt.tools`                          | N/A                              | Tool definitions - no direct OTEL equivalent                  | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.prompt.toolChoice`                     | N/A                              | Tool choice setting - no direct OTEL equivalent               | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.response.toolCalls`                    | N/A                              | **DEPRECATED** - Use Event API to report tool calls           | ⚠️ Deprecated             |
| `ai.response.msToFirstChunk`               | N/A                              | Streaming-specific timing - no direct OTEL equivalent         | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.response.msToFinish`                   | N/A                              | Streaming-specific timing - no direct OTEL equivalent         | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.response.avgCompletionTokensPerSecond` | N/A                              | Streaming-specific metrics - no direct OTEL equivalent        | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.schema`                                | N/A                              | JSON schema for object generation - no direct OTEL equivalent | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.schema.name`                           | N/A                              | Schema name - no direct OTEL equivalent                       | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.schema.description`                    | N/A                              | Schema description - no direct OTEL equivalent                | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.response.object`                       | N/A                              | Generated object - no direct OTEL equivalent                  | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.settings.mode`                         | `gen_ai.output.type`             | Output type (e.g., `json`, `text`)                            | 🔄 Needs mapping          |
| `ai.settings.output`                       | N/A                              | Output format setting - no direct OTEL equivalent             | ➖ No mapping needed      |
| `ai.settings.maxSteps`                     | N/A                              | Max steps setting - no direct OTEL equivalent                 | ➖ No mapping needed      |

## Operation Name Mappings

| **Vercel AI SDK Operation** | **OpenTelemetry Operation**                 | **Notes**                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `ai.generateText`           | `gen_ai.operation.name: "chat"`             | Text generation operation    |
| `ai.streamText`             | `gen_ai.operation.name: "chat"`             | Streaming text generation    |
| `ai.generateObject`         | `gen_ai.operation.name: "generate_content"` | Structured object generation |
| `ai.streamObject`           | `gen_ai.operation.name: "generate_content"` | Streaming object generation  |
| `ai.embed`                  | `gen_ai.operation.name: "embeddings"`       | Embedding generation         |
| `ai.embedMany`              | `gen_ai.operation.name: "embeddings"`       | Batch embedding generation   |
| `ai.toolCall`               | `gen_ai.operation.name: "execute_tool"`     | Tool execution               |

## GenAI Request Parameters

These Vercel AI SDK parameters should be mapped to standard OTEL GenAI request parameters:

| **Vercel AI SDK Attribute**        | **OpenTelemetry Attribute**        | **Notes**                    |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `gen_ai.request.temperature`       | `gen_ai.request.temperature`       | Already using OTEL attribute |
| `gen_ai.request.max_tokens`        | `gen_ai.request.max_tokens`        | Already using OTEL attribute |
| `gen_ai.request.frequency_penalty` | `gen_ai.request.frequency_penalty` | Already using OTEL attribute |
| `gen_ai.request.presence_penalty`  | `gen_ai.request.presence_penalty`  | Already using OTEL attribute |
| `gen_ai.request.top_k`             | `gen_ai.request.top_k`             | Already using OTEL attribute |
| `gen_ai.request.top_p`             | `gen_ai.request.top_p`             | Already using OTEL attribute |
| `gen_ai.request.stop_sequences`    | `gen_ai.request.stop_sequences`    | Already using OTEL attribute |

## Legend

- ✅ Already mapped in code
- 🔄 Needs mapping
- ➖ No mapping needed
- ⚠️ Deprecated

hey, I just found how to do this. Edit model works fine again when I disabled reasoning on reasoningable model like gpt5.4. If you have a openai-compatible model, edit your config.yaml like:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
  - name: gpt-5.4-mini
    provider: openai
    model: gpt-5.4-mini
    apiKey: x
    apiBase: x
    roles:
      - edit
    requestOptions:
      extraBodyProperties:
        reasoning:
          effort: none
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

body:
Okay so after a bit more digging I have the following other info:
(1) Looks like the Azure provider is a pretty thin wrapper on the OpenAi provider, which is problematic because the Azure Open AI service handles attachments differently [according to this page,](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/reasoning?tabs=gpt-5%2Cpython%2Cpy#availability) but haven't dug so much into that yet.
(2) Bigger issue is that the OpenAI provider only enumerates a few types of allowed files and reject all other files, even if the underlaying model might support it. [See here.](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/openai/src/chat/convert-to-openai-chat-messages.ts#L65). As of 2.0.28 the file type needs to match image/* audio/* or application/pdf, otherwise an error is thrown before even trying to hit the model.

- One quick fix would be to loosen the check around (2) and *try* to make the API request and let the request fail if its truly unsupported, or update those checks to more closely match the actual model capabilities, but I imagine thats a bit like playing whackamole
- ^ But this might only fix the OpenAi provider not the issues caused by (1). Fixing Azure would require a deeper understanding of the differences with how their hosted OpenAI models behave differently, which I know contain some other limitations right now (such as lack of support for web_search tool). 


For now, I will likely have to go back to using the OpenAI provider directly to hope PDFs work (sorry to my Azure credits 😔) and pull the contents of the plain/text file into the the messages directly.  Will also need to pull contents of CSVs and other files into the message directly.

body:
I investigated this issue and tested with Azure/OpenAI API. The error occurs because **OpenAI/Azure responses API only supports PDF files** (not text/plain). [openai file upload](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/pdf-files?api-mode=responses)

According to Azure's documentation:
-  Chat API: Supports `image/*`, `audio/*`, `application/pdf` only [azure responses](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/responses?tabs=python-key#file-input)
-  File Search API: Supports `text/plain`, `.md`, `.txt`, etc. [azure file search](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/file-search?tabs=python#supported-file-types)

The SDK's error is correct.

Should we update the documentation to clarify which file types are compatible with which OpenAI/ Azure APIs?

@gr2m thoughts?

For anyone experiencing this issue, it is caused by using `experimental_continueSteps: true`. 

The relevant code can be found [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/ed0ebebeca0733f00638c8460d37a4e9c0a573c7/packages/ai/core/generate-text/stream-text.ts#L1162). While likely a logic bug, this behavior is acceptable given the 'experimental' nature of the feature.

body:
> Where do these suggestions come from?

The are defined in the provider code, e.g. https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7756857e2bf30c81293eb2e3bbae343a496a2731/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-options.ts

We are not planning export the list of supported models as array. Right now they are just types which doesn't have any impact on the final code run in production. We would 

1. Need to define the supported model IDs across all providers (both our own and community provider npm packages) as JS Arrays (bundle size impact)
2. We would need to infer the types from that array (TypeScript performance impact)

Instead, you can assume we just support all latest models from all providers. And if we miss one, that's a bug and we welcome your PR to fix it.

Longer term, we are looking into creating a registry which monitors changes from all the providers we support, including the list of model IDs. We would than use these list to generate our types, but you could probably use the same lists programatically for your app. We have an early version of that which currently only monitors some provider OpenAPI specs: https://github.com/gr2m/ai-provider-monitor. But watch that space, we will add monitoring for supported models by providers soon

body:
- Structured output, so it can be used as code, composable.

**Usage**

```bash
$ curl -s https://acme.com/pricing | \
  npx ai "extract pricing tiers" --schema '{
    "tiers": [{
      "name": "string",
      "price": "number",
      "bandwidth_gb": "number",
      "team_members": "number"
    }]
  }'
```

Output:

```json
{
  "tiers": [
    {"name": "Starter", "price": 0, "bandwidth_gb": 50, "team_members": 1},
    {"name": "Growth", "price": 29, "bandwidth_gb": 500, "team_members": 5},
    {"name": "Scale", "price": 99, "bandwidth_gb": 2000, "team_members": 20},
    {"name": "Enterprise", "price": -1, "bandwidth_gb": -1, "team_members": -1}
  ]
}
```

**Advanced usage** – solving harder problems with AI as an API blackbox

Ex: Installing the latest version of a github release is trickier than it may seem, but it could become something like:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# install-latest.sh - Install any GitHub CLI tool with one command

REPO=$1  # e.g., "junegunn/fzf"

# Get latest release data
curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest" | \
  npx ai "find download URL for $(uname -s) $(uname -m)" --schema '{
    "download_url": "string",
    "binary_name": "string",
    "extract_command": "string"
  }' > release.json

# Extract the info
URL=$(jq -r .download_url release.json)
BINARY=$(jq -r .binary_name release.json)
EXTRACT=$(jq -r .extract_command release.json)

# Download and install
curl -L "$URL" -o /tmp/download
eval "$EXTRACT” # 🤠
chmod +x "$BINARY"

I am not sure if this is of any value to the development team here but based on these comments I was able to solve this same problem in a different framework.

A request that includes encrypted reasoning will always produce this error if the input contains an item without an id that was generated immediately after the reasoning item. Of course this is important with tool calls but if you send the reasoning item explicitly in a subsequent request then the problem will occur even if the item is web search, code interpreter or even just text.

I suspect most can solve their issue by dropping the encrypted reasoning item for any subsequent explicit requests ( not, as many recommend here, by copying the response verbatim into a subsequent call ).

body:
## Different Root Cause: Backpressure Leading to Same Error

I encountered the same error message ("Item 'rs_...' of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item") but with a different root cause in my case.

**My scenario:**
- Using Vercel AI SDK v5 with OpenAI Responses API (`gpt-5`)
- Client-side tool execution generating long SQL queries
- 5-12 tool calls per user request, each producing hundreds of `tool-input-delta` events
- Complex React application (React Query, Toast, etc.)

**What happened:**
The stream would stop mid-execution with no errors (HTTP 200, no console/server logs). The next message send would trigger the "reasoning" 400 error.

**Root cause:**
Backpressure from React re-rendering. The massive number of streaming events (1000+ for multiple tool calls with long SQL generation) overwhelmed React's rendering capacity. The ReadableStream buffer filled up, TCP flow control kicked in, and the server eventually timed out and closed the connection normally (HTTP 200).

This left incomplete reasoning parts in message history, causing the 400 error on the next request.

**Solution:**
Adding `experimental_throttle: 100` to `useChat`:

```typescript
const { messages, sendMessage, status, addToolResult } = useChat({
  experimental_throttle: 100, // Batch updates every 100ms
  // ...
});
```

This reduced re-renders from 1000+ to ~60, allowing the stream to complete successfully.

**Why it's tricky:**
- No errors appear (HTTP 200, stream closes normally)
- Only fails in complex apps (simple reproductions work fine due to faster re-rendering)
- Same error message as #7099 but different underlying issue (backpressure vs SDK bug)

Hope this helps others debugging similar symptoms!
author: coji

body:
# Additional Root Cause: Zod Validation Failures

We encountered the same error intermittently:

```
Item 'rs_xxx' of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item.
```

**Root cause in our case: Zod schema validation failures in tool definitions.**

## The Core Issue

**OpenAI validates tool arguments server-side against your Zod schemas before your tool executes.** When validation fails with GPT-5:

1. Model generates reasoning items
2. Model calls a tool with invalid arguments
3. OpenAI's server rejects the tool call (validation fails)
4. Request fails with 400 error - **your tool never executes, model never sees the error**
5. Reasoning item left without a valid "following item" (the rejected tool call)

This is intermittent because the model sometimes generates valid arguments, sometimes doesn't.

## Our Setup

- GPT-5 via Vercel AI SDK `streamText()`
- Tool calling with Zod input schemas
- Using `previousResponseId` (though unclear if this is required to trigger the bug)
- ai@5.0.89, @ai-sdk/openai@2.0.64

## Reproduction

Force validation to always fail:

```typescript
inputSchema: z.object({
  param: z.string().refine(() => false, 'Always fails')
})
```

Result: 100% reproduction of the reasoning error.

## Workaround

Move validation from schema to execution so model receives the error and can retry:

```typescript
// Before (breaks reasoning chain)
inputSchema: z.object({
  timestamp: z.string().regex(/^\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3}$/)
})

// After (model sees error, can retry in same turn)
inputSchema: z.object({
  timestamp: z.string()
}),
execute: async ({ timestamp }) => {
  if (!/^\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3}$/.test(timestamp)) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid format: ${timestamp}`);
  }
}
```

**Bottom line:** Avoid regex, refine, transform in tool schemas when using GPT-5. Move all validation into the `execute` function.

Thanks for raising this issue.

I’d like to add some additional context regarding the current OpenAI API capabilities, which may support expanding the allowed media types here.

According to the official OpenAI documentation for file inputs:
https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/file-inputs

Spreadsheet formats such as the following are explicitly listed as supported input types:

- .csv  (MIME: text/csv)
- .xls
- .xlsx (MIME: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Allowing these spreadsheet media types in `@ai-sdk/openai` would help align the SDK with the provider's documented functionality and make it easier to pass structured data (especially CSV/XLSX) directly to models without additional preprocessing.

As a small additional note: the same OpenAI documentation also lists common document formats such as `.docx` and `.pptx` as supported file inputs. Supporting those MIME types as well would be very helpful for document-oriented workflows. 

Of course, this suggestion is specifically about the OpenAI provider — other providers may have different supported file types.

Thanks again for the work on the AI SDK!

body:
In case it helps future research:

The API key is set as the `Authorization` header on the request to bedrock
e.g. `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`

The AWS JS SDK checks for the `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` environment variable, and uses that if present. The Vercel AI Bedrock provider doesn't use the AWS JS SDK, but might want to follow this convention. 

[AWS Docs - Use an Amazon Bedrock API Key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-use.html)

An example curl request to demonstrate the request structure
```sh
#!/bin/sh

URL="https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0/converse"
API_KEY="redacted"
PAYLOAD='{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Hello"}]}]}'


curl $URL \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -d "$PAYLOAD"

```

body:
## Microsoft Learn MCP Server Compatibility Issue

I've been testing the SSE transport with Microsoft's official MCP server at `https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp` and found a specific compatibility issue that affects remote MCP server support.

### The Problem
The current AI SDK SSE transport implementation fails with **405 Method Not Allowed** when connecting to Microsoft's MCP server:

```javascript
const client = await experimental_createMCPClient({
  name: "microsoft-docs",
  transport: {
    type: "sse",
    url: "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp",
  },
});
// Error: MCP SSE Transport Error: 405 Method Not Allowed
```

### Root Cause Analysis

**Standard SSE Protocol**: Uses GET method with `Accept: text/event-stream`
**Microsoft MCP Server**: Requires POST method with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`

### Evidence

1. **AI SDK correctly uses GET** (standard SSE):
   ```bash
   # This is what AI SDK sends (correctly per SSE spec)
   GET https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp
   Accept: text/event-stream
   ```

2. **Microsoft server only accepts POST**:
   ```bash
   curl -I "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp"
   # HTTP/2 405 Method Not Allowed
   # allow: POST
   ```

3. **Microsoft server works with POST + dual Accept headers**:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp" \
     -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize", "params": {...}}'
   # Returns: event: message / data: {...}
   ```

### Proposed Enhancement

Add configuration options to the SSE transport for non-standard MCP implementations:

```typescript
transport: {
  type: "sse",
  url: "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp",
  method: "POST", // Allow POST for non-standard servers
  headers: {
    "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"
  }
}
```

This would maintain backward compatibility while enabling support for Microsoft's MCP server and potentially other non-standard SSE implementations.

### Impact
This affects integration with Microsoft's official documentation MCP server, which is a significant use case for developers building AI applications that need access to Microsoft Learn content.

**Related**: opencode (which uses AI SDK 5.0.0-beta.7) experiences this same issue - sst/opencode#834

body:
If you have been experiencing this, it's because you're using legacy tsconfig settings, namely `moduleResolution: "node"`. There's no reason to be using this anymore. The root cause was a very subtle resolution bug that caused both ESM and CJS versions of Zod to be loaded in the codebase simultaneously. TypeScript considers these independent constructs, resulting in  assignability issues and associated slow TS performance and occasionally OOM errors.

The simplest fix for this is to upgrade to a modern `moduleResolution` setting: https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#moduleResolution. The old `"node"` setting mirrored the behavior of Node 10 which hit EOL in 2021.

That said, I found a mitigation on Zod's end that also resolves this issue. Upgrade to `zod@4.1.6` and you won't hit this anymore: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5222

body:
Hi @lgrammel,

I'm currently using a fully manual agent loop, roughly following this flow:
1. The user sends a message over WebSocket.
2. We ping an API, which schedules a message on the event bus for our agent to process.
3. The agent starts processing the message.
4. Once processing is complete, we persist the new message and send it back over WebSocket.

The streams generated inside the `for await` loop (where we consume the UI stream) are piped through our WebSocket server and displayed to the user in the UI.

Since these messages are always rendered in the UI, we want to persist them in our database using the `UIMessage` schema instead of the `ModelMessage` schema, as the latter wouldn’t make sense for UI display purposes.

Initially, I looked into using `ModelMessage`, as that’s the recommended approach for the manual agent loop in the docs (https://ai-sdk.dev/cookbook/node/manual-agent-loop). However, I have a Next.js app and a Chrome extension that both render these messages, and using `UIMessage` to display them is much more convenient (even though I’m not using useChat, it gives me a good baseline interface).

Since my use case is quite custom - unlike what others have described in this issue thread, I was just sharing my current hacky solution 😅 for getting `UIMessages` from the streamText. Previously, I would await the `response.message`, then use `appendResponseMessages` to get the persistable `UIMessages` and save them to the database.

body:
@lgrammel, thanks for your attention on this issue. This may not be the proper venue for such a discussion, but I wanted to share some observations from the past couple of months of using the AI SDK to build production apps with both headless and UI-based flows.

**What's working exceptionally well:**
The AI SDK is an extremely strong framework for building with AI. The developer experience is unmatched, primarily due to how it leverages the TypeScript type system. It's clear that type safety has been a driving force behind not only the implementation but also the **opinionated ontology** of the framework—and this opinionation is actually a strength when you understand it.

**Where friction occurs:**
New users (including myself and others who have contributed to this issue) often hit roadblocks where we suddenly perceive massive oversights or missing features that seem to make the SDK unusable for our chosen paradigms. In reality, these are often misalignments between our mental models and the framework's intentionally opinionated design.

**A suggestion:**
Since the SDK's power comes from its opinionated nature, it would be helpful if this ontology and the reasoning behind key architectural decisions could be more explicitly documented. A clear articulation of the framework's opinions would help developers:
- Understand which patterns the SDK is optimized for (and which it intentionally doesn't support)
- Align their application architecture with the framework's design philosophy from the start
- Recognize when they're fighting against the framework rather than working with it

This transparency about the SDK's opinions would prevent developers from investing significant time in approaches that conflict with its core design principles, turning what initially feels like "missing features" into conscious trade-offs we can plan around.

body:
We're also facing this issue in our evaluation system where we use `generateText` for batch processing questions through background jobs.

### Our use case

- We have a background job system that processes multiple questions in batches
- Each question is sent to `generateText` API to get AI-generated answers
- We need to persist these messages to database for later review in the UI
- The messages contain tool calls (knowledge base queries) that we need to extract citations from

### Current challenge

- `generateText` returns `ResponseMessage[]` via `result.response.messages`
- We need to store these as messages that can be displayed in UI components
- There's no built-in way to convert `ResponseMessage[]` to `UIMessage[]`

### What we need

A `convertToUIMessages()` utility function (inverse of `convertToModelMessages()`) that can:
- Convert `ResponseMessage[]` from `generateText` to `UIMessage[]`
- Preserve tool call information and results
- Make it easy to persist and later display messages in UI

This would be especially helpful for headless/background processing scenarios where `streamText` isn't practical but we still need UI-compatible message format for storage and display.

body:
Opened #15379 with a `convertToUIMessages(messages, { generateId? })` utility — the inverse of `convertToModelMessages`.

Scope of the first version:
- system / user / assistant messages → one `UIMessage` each (id generated via the provided/default `generateId`)
- tool messages are merged into the preceding assistant message's matching tool-call part by `toolCallId`, transitioning state to `output-available` / `output-error` / `output-denied` based on the tool-result output shape
- text, reasoning, tool-call/tool-result, and file (URL + provider-reference) parts handled
- custom parts, reasoning-file parts, tool-approval-request parts, and inline byte file data are intentionally scoped out — documented in the JSDoc and PR description as candidates for follow-ups

Tests cover all three tool-result state transitions, orphan tool-calls, and the missing-preceding-assistant error path.

@paulonasc we have moved to langgraph. I can't say it was a great decision, but at least we no longer have this issue. However, we have got a lot of other problems. Here is my list of pros/cons of LangGraph compared to AI SDK:

**Pros**
1. You don't have this issue 😆 
2. A lot of tutorials and examples
3. More control
4. Agentic workflows (however, I've recently discovered [voltagent](https://github.com/VoltAgent/voltagent) that should cover this gap for the AI SDK. I haven't tested it, though)

**Cons**
1. Langgraph is pushing its approaches and services on the backend. For example, "checkpointers", langgraph cli, langsmith, etc.
2. LangGraph does not fully abstract LLM model responses. If you want to use models from different providers, you have to convert messages to the appropriate format. E.g., you can't use the response from Anthropic models and send them to Gemini to summarize. It will fail because the messages are incompatible, despite being instances of AIMessage provided by LangGraph (LangChain).
3.  LangGraph is focused on the backend use cases (e.g., offline workflows). Their frontend support is not so great.

From the ease/usability perspective, the AI SDK is a clear winner here. However, it lacks multi-agent capabilities and has this nasty bug that forced us to move. We were early in the development, so it was not hard for us to do.

By the way, are you also using NestJS (not Next) for the backend or something different? I want to understand if this has something to do with it.

body: In our case, this ended up being because Vercel uses OpenAI's Requests API by default, instead of Chat Completions. The Requests API will randomly provide multiple "versions" of its output (there seems to be no way to disable this and there are complaints about this all over the OpenAI forums). When in "streaming" mode, these versions come through as "text-delta" events with different IDs. If you've previously been using the Chat Completions API, this doesn't happen. To solve the problem, we look at the first text-delta ID we receive and make sure to only stream other text-delta's with the same ID. Hope this helps someone!

body:
For anyone encountering this issue with the error message in the title, check the provider source code to understand the expected behavior for handling `FileUIPart` in the user message. For instance, the `openai` provider will handle:
* Image as either 1) `URL` object; 2) base64 encoded URL as a string; or 3) `Uint8Array`, which will be converted to a base64 encoded URL by the library.
* Audio files in wav/mp3/mpeg format as `Uint8Array`, which will be converted to a base64 encoded URL by the library.
* PDF files as a base64 encoded URL in a string or `Uint8Array`.
