body:
If you have been experiencing this, it's because you're using legacy tsconfig settings, namely `moduleResolution: "node"`. There's no reason to be using this anymore. The root cause was a very subtle resolution bug that caused both ESM and CJS versions of Zod to be loaded in the codebase simultaneously. TypeScript considers these independent constructs, resulting in  assignability issues and associated slow TS performance and occasionally OOM errors.

The simplest fix for this is to upgrade to a modern `moduleResolution` setting: https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#moduleResolution. The old `"node"` setting mirrored the behavior of Node 10 which hit EOL in 2021.

That said, I found a mitigation on Zod's end that also resolves this issue. Upgrade to `zod@4.1.6` and you won't hit this anymore: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5222

body:
> I encountered a related issue when upgrading from AI SDK v4 to v5 that might provide additional context.
> 
> ## Context
> Processing emails that may contain multiple data items using `generateObject` with Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
> 
> **Schema definition:**
> 
> const schema = z.object({
>   title: z.string(),
>   content: z.string(),
>   metadata: z.object({
>     // ... other fields
>   })
> });
> **Observed behavior across different version combinations:**
> 
> AI SDK	Zod	Result
> v4.3.19	v3.25.76	Success - returns first item only, no errors
> v5.0.0-beta.25	v4.0.5	Error - JSON parsing failed
> v5.0.0-beta.25	v3.25.76	Error - JSON parsing failed (same as v5+v4)
> **Error details (v5 with both Zod v3 and v4):**
> 
> ```
> AI_NoObjectGeneratedError: No object generated: could not parse the response
> JSON parsing failed: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position ...
> ```
> 
> **What Claude actually returned:** When the input contained multiple items, Claude returned multiple tool_use calls:
> 
> {
>   "content": [
>     {
>       "type": "tool_use",
>       "id": "toolu_01...",
>       "name": "json",
>       "input": { "title": "Item 1", "content": "...", ... }
>     },
>     {
>       "type": "tool_use", 
>       "id": "toolu_02...",
>       "name": "json",
>       "input": { "title": "Item 2", "content": "...", ... }
>     },
>     {
>       "type": "tool_use",
>       "id": "toolu_03...",
>       "name": "json",
>       "input": { "title": "Item 3", "content": "...", ... }
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ## Resolution
> Updated schema to handle arrays:
> 
> const schema = z.object({
>   items: z.array(z.object({
>     title: z.string(),
>     content: z.string(),
>     metadata: z.object({
>       // ... other fields
>     })
>   }))
> });
> ### Possible explanation for the behavior difference
> Looking at the error details, it seems like:
> 
> * **v4**: When Claude returns multiple tool_use calls, the SDK might only process the first tool_use's input, which happens to match our single object schema
> * **v5**: The SDK appears to concatenate all tool_use inputs into a single string (`{...}{...}{...}`), which fails JSON parsing when it encounters the second object immediately after the first
> 
> ## Summary
> The issue appears to be specific to how the AI SDK handles multiple tool_use responses from Claude. In v4, it silently processed only the first item. In v5, it fails with a parsing error regardless of Zod version. The array schema approach works correctly in both versions and captures all data.

Nice insights.

This feels like a temporary solution though, or is this standard expected behaviour from now on?

TypeScript considers these independent constructs, resulting in  assignability issues and associated slow TS performance and occasionally OOM errors.

The simplest fix for this is to upgrade to a modern `moduleResolution` setting: https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#moduleResolution. The old `"node"` setting mirrored the behavior of Node 10 which hit EOL in 2021.

That said, I found a mitigation on Zod's end that also resolves this issue. Upgrade to `zod@4.1.6` and you won't hit this anymore: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5222

body:
I tried this out and was having issues. Turns out mine were with my load balancer. But the protocol has also changed and the example hasn't been updated to reflect that. Check the docs here: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/stream-protocol#data-stream-protocol

Here's an example of what you have to do now:

```python
import asyncio
import json
import uuid

async def event_stream():
    message_id = f"msg_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    
    yield f'data: {json.dumps({"type": "start", "messageId": message_id})}\n\n'
    
    text_id = f"text_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    yield f'data: {json.dumps({"type": "text-start", "id": text_id})}\n\n'
    
    chunks = ["This", " is", " a", " test", " response"]
    for chunk in chunks:
        yield f'data: {json.dumps({"type": "text-delta", "id": text_id, "delta": chunk})}\n\n'
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    
    yield f'data: {json.dumps({"type": "text-end", "id": text_id})}\n\n'
    yield f'data: {json.dumps({"type": "finish"})}\n\n'
    yield f'data: [DONE]\n\n'
```

Took me longer than I would have liked to get this working -- hope this saves someone else some time!

Edit: make sure you add the custom headers: `{"x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream": "v1"}` -- won't work without it

body:
Hey 👋 thanks for bringing this up! I can explain what's happening here.

## The "delay" you're seeing

The status changes to "streaming" as soon as the connection to the server is established and streaming begins - this includes metadata streaming, not just the LLM's generated tokens. So there's a natural delay between:
1. Connection established + metadata streaming starts → `status = "streaming"`  
2. First actual token from the LLM arrives → user sees content

This is why you see "streaming" status but no rendered content yet - it's technically streaming (metadata and data parts if you have any), just not the content you're expecting.

## Replicating the old behavior

If you'd like to replicate the loading behavior from before, you could create a variable that remains true until message parts actually contain content:

```javascript
const lastMessage = messages.at(-1);

const showLoader = 
  status === "streaming" && 
  lastMessage?.role === "assistant" && 
  lastMessage?.parts?.length === 0; // replace with a .some check for a specific part type you're waiting for (e.g. `text`, `data-someData` etc.)
```

---

Given this is application-specific behavior, we're going to hold off making any API changes just yet. The current `status` accurately reflects the technical streaming state. How you interpret that for your UI is up to your specific use case.

Your workaround is exactly the right approach - using the status plus additional checks to create the loading experience you want!

body:
If you have been experiencing this, it's because you're using legacy tsconfig settings, namely `moduleResolution: "node"`. There's no reason to be using this anymore. The root cause was a very subtle resolution bug that caused both ESM and CJS versions of Zod to be loaded in the codebase simultaneously. TypeScript considers these independent constructs, resulting in  assignability issues and associated slow TS performance and occasionally OOM errors.

The simplest fix for this is to upgrade to a modern `moduleResolution` setting: https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#moduleResolution. The old `"node"` setting mirrored the behavior of Node 10 which hit EOL in 2021.

That said, I found a mitigation on Zod's end that also resolves this issue. Upgrade to `zod@4.1.6` and you won't hit this anymore: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5222

body:
I'm running into this when combining tool calling with extended thinking. Both work fine when used without the other, but when the llm tries to call a tool, I see this error immediately after the tool call completes.

Here's the ordering of things I'm seeing in the AI stream:
1. start
2. start-step
3. reasoning-start
4. reasoning-delta
5. tool-input-start - Tool call begins (toolName: "search")
6. tool-input-delta
7. tool-input-available
8. reasoning-end
9. tool-output-available
10. finish-step
11. error - Anthropic API rejects the second request

So it seems like it errors here because there's no thinking step ending this message.

I asked opus 4 to analyze this with `ai` codebase context...not sure how accurate this is but maybe sheds some light? Sorry if it's just slop lol.

~~~

When the AI SDK prepares the second API call (after tool execution), it reconstructs the assistant message from these parts. The SDK internally converts:
- reasoning-delta parts → thinking block
- tool-input-* parts → tool_use block

However, because the tool-input parts appear BETWEEN the reasoning-delta and reasoning-end parts, the SDK likely processes them in that order, resulting in:

Assistant message content: [
  { type: 'tool_use', ... },    // From tool-input parts
  { type: 'thinking', ... }      // From reasoning-delta parts
]

Anthropic's API requires that when extended thinking is enabled, thinking blocks MUST precede tool_use blocks. The error confirms this: "When thinking is enabled, a final assistant message must start with a thinking block (preceding the lastmost set of tool_use and tool_result blocks)".

The SDK needs to reorder these blocks to satisfy Anthropic's requirement, regardless of the order they were streamed.

~~~

body:
When you encounter this issue, please check the following:

a) are you using prepareStep to change the messages?
b) are you using a stream transformation (in particular custom ones)?
c) are you using a provider other than `@ai-sdk/anthropic`?

All of these can be related to the issue. The AI SDK stores additional information in the provider metadata (here: Anthropic reasoning signatures) that are required by the Anthropic API if you want to send reasoning parts back. If this information gets changes or some of it is lost or other parts of the messages object change, there is a risk that the Anthropic API will reject it.

body:
Opened #15380 with a fix.

Root cause: `useChat` creates `Chat` once via `new Chat(optionsWithCallbacks)` and the transport gets captured there. Inline transports closing over component state never refresh.

Fix: apply the same `callbacksRef` pattern already used in this hook for `onFinish` / `onError` / `onToolCall` — keep the user's transport in a ref, pass `Chat` a stable delegating proxy whose `sendMessages` / `reconnectToStream` read through to the latest ref value. No API change on `Chat`; the proxy lives on the React side only.

Regression test mirrors the exact issue body: state → `useState`, transport built inline with `body: { state }`, button toggles state, sendMessage's request body asserts the latest value.

body:
@lgrammel, no, I think it's still an issue. I'm not 100% sure what the right fix is, but I think updating `extractReasoningMiddleware` to omit whitespace text parts is the root fix. This is non-trivial though I'm guessing because for streaming text the order is:

1. LLM responds
2. text-start part is streamed
3. `extractReasoningMiddleware` kicks in and instead of streaming text-delta part it streams reasoning parts
4. whatever is left or maybe by default "\n" (that's what I'm seeing) is streamed as text-delta
5. text-end part is pushed.

So what needs to happen is if `extractReasoningMiddleware` is used we need to hold off on step 2 until we know there is non-reasoning text, but we won't know if we need to do that until `extractReasoningMiddleware` finishes with the entire response from LLM to know if there is no text. I think the issue is that the responses I'm seeing from Nova models are all `<thinking>` and `extractReasoningMiddleware` assumed there would be some text. Or maybe Nova is the only model that throws error if whitespace/empty text.

Yeah I think that would be a great utility function, but it's a nice to have an is a bit outside the scope for core features of the SDK. What you're describing is content manipulation of the final output of the model. This would be the same thing someone would have to build if the system prompt to any model included, `...think to yourself and plan your course of action before responding to the user. Separate these thoughts from the rest of your response by placing these thoughts in <for_my_eyes_only> tags`

`extractReasoningMiddleware` extracts content from the reasoning part of the model response, which is only available on reasoning models, which Amazon Nova is not. 

To see this in action, enable Bedrock Invocation logging in CloudWatch and then invoke Bedrock via your app, the CLI, or the Console. Do it once for Amazon Nova, and another time for Claude Sonnet with Reasoning turned on. Then compare the output JSON format of the two responses. `extractReasoningMiddleware` looks for the specific object that you'll see present only in the Claude response.

body:
> extractReasoningMiddleware extracts content from the reasoning part of the model response, which is only available on reasoning models, which Amazon Nova is not.

Based on my experience this is not true. It extracts `<thinking>` tags from Amazon Nova's text response and adds them as reasoning parts in AI SDK's `UIMessage`.

See definition [here](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/extract-reasoning-middleware):

> extractReasoningMiddleware is a middleware function that extracts XML-tagged reasoning sections from generated text and exposes them separately from the main text content.
author: bestickley

body:
🤦 oops yeah my bad, you're correct about `extractReasoningMiddleware` 

When are you getting this error? Is it when Nova doesn't respond with `<thinking>` tags? Nova models do not reliably respond with `<thinking>` tags. I've tried several different approaches and I cannot reproduce any of your issues. What/when is your custom `convertMessages()` being used for? Are you storing your messages as valid `UIMessage[]` in your persistence layer?

If you're using your `convertMessages()` function to prepare messages to send to model, you shouldn't. You can send `UIMessage[]` with valid `ReasoningPart[]` to the SDK's `convertToModelMessages()` function and send the output of that to Nova models. You don't need to add custom logic there. But if it's because you're noticing that when you use the SDK's convert function, the reasoning steps aren't being sent to Bedrock...

> For my use case (and many I'd think), I want the reasoning as context for the model on subsequent requests so my above workaround of wrapping reasoning in thinking tags work for me

...then that's something different. If reasoning context is important for your workload, you should probably be using a reasoning model. Generally, reasoning context is not very valuable to models not trained to be reasoning models, and if anything, pollutes the context. Opinions differ on this, but some go as far as to say that you shouldn't even include previous reasoning steps in successive LLM invocations to reasoning models. Usually the model's response is pretty representative of the reasoning, too, which can easily be inferred by the model.

All this to say, if you've observed that your workload objectively works better with full, reasoning-included, context, you should run those workloads on reasoning models vs. mocking reasoning to non-reasoning models.

I'd probably keep the raw text, including `<thinking>` tags in all `UIMessages`, without extracting it to `ReasoningPart` and apply XML regex on the frontend to hide content from the user. iirc, this is what Anthropic does in some capacity for the Claude.ai UI with their `<ant...>` tags

Rationale: The issue describes a concrete runtime failure in current AI SDK behavior when middleware-generated empty/whitespace text parts are converted and sent to Amazon Nova, causing provider errors. Although workarounds and possible fixes are discussed, the primary report is broken behavior.

@lgrammel  You can see now how this issue propagates further down the dependency chain as @longsman  has shown above: 

Now any software that doesn't update a package and push a release on day-1 doesn't allow their users to use the new models properly.

They're all blocked by:
1. Vercel must update the AI SDK
2. The software developers updating their version of the ai sdk and pushing a new release
3. The user must download that release

It should just be as simple as changing the model name, as the package advertises as a core feature, but now it's not.

This actually greatly reduces accessibility to models rather than increasing it like the package is designed to do.

body:
### Identify issue type

**Identified type: Bug**  
Confidence: High

Rationale: The issue reports a concrete regression/failure in existing SDK behavior: `addToolResult` does not apply results for MCP dynamic tools in v5, breaking human-in-the-loop flows that worked in v4. Although comments mention missing dynamic-tool support and workarounds, the core report is broken current behavior.

Evidence:
- Reporter says `addToolResult` worked in AI SDK v4 but stopped after upgrading to v5 for MCP tools.
- Calling `addToolResult({ tool, toolCallId, output })` followed by `sendMessage()` leaves the tool information unchanged, while normal tools work.
- Reporter and commenters identify MCP invocations as `dynamic-tool`, with `addToolResult` not handling those parts; a workaround is to convert/wrap MCP dynamic tools as normal tools.
- A commenter points to `isToolUIPart` failing for dynamic tool parts, so the result is never added.

Yes, sir! ✅💯
You are 100% correct. ✅💯
@draklorx

We shouldn't keep the API token on the frontend.

<details>

<summary>Explanation:</summary>

The API key shouldn't be accessible on the frontend side.

So, there are 2 ways to solve this:

Vocabulary:

- Provider: OpenAI, Gemini, ....
- Server: Your server. ExpressJS, Django or NestJS, ...ect
- Client: User's app: React, React Native ....

### Solutions:

1. Client to server approach (Recommended):

- The API key is maintained on the backend server application (Express for example).
- THe server has an endpoint to generate an temporary token and limited, called "Ephemeral Token". and the endpoint can return this ephemeral token to client
- The client sends a request to backend to get the ephemeral token
- The Client uses the ephemeral token to communicate with the AI provider (Gemini or OpenAI, ...) instead of using the API key
- The ephemeral token will expire

2. Server to Server (Not recommended)

- The server has the API key
- The client opens a Websocket with the server
- the server opens a websocket with the provider
- Request: client => server => provided
- Response: client <= server =< provider
- this is not recommended for latency

</details>

---

@lgrammel told me to keep everything in one relevant thread [in this comment](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/4082#issuecomment-3219151987). That's why I stopped posting any updates here. 🌹

body:
@flexchar I'm not familiar with your exact situation, but something that looks similar to the following is how I'd handle a semi-long lived api change:
* [assuming you're working with node] include both dependencies in your server; npm/pnpm has aliases https://pnpm.io/aliases that lets you have both v4 and v5 versions in the same project
* use a new endpoint for the v5 functionality, and leave the old endpoint untouched; or add an optional header that only new clients send, e.g. `x-vercel-format: data`, `x-vercel-version: 5`
* put some logging or telemetry on the old v4 endpoint and when activity is low enough, remove the v4 handling

Your new client (chrome extension) should only need the new v5 client.

body:
I got the same issue as well. Here's a small investigation done by my IDE.

-----

## AI SDK OpenAI Provider - Persistent Reasoning Artifacts Bug

### Summary

When using the AI SDK's OpenAI provider with reasoningEffort enabled (e.g., medium), the provider appears to persist reasoning artifacts (rs_* items) in a way that causes subsequent API calls to fail with a 400 Bad Request error from OpenAI's Responses API.

Error Message:

`LLMRequestError: Item 'rs_...' of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item.`

### Investigation Findings

**1. Clean Input Messages**: We verified via deep debug logging that the messages array passed to streamText is "clean" - it contains only text and tool-call parts. No reasoning parts are present in the input.

Log Trace (Input to streamText):
```
[
  {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": [
      { "type": "text", "text": "" },
      { "type": "tool-call", "toolCallId": "call_...", "toolName": "...", "input": {} }
    ]
  },
  {
    "role": "tool",
    "content": [
      { "type": "tool-result", "toolCallId": "call_...", "toolName": "...", "result": "..." }
    ]
  }
]
```

**2. Persistence of Hidden State**: Despite the clean input, the OpenAI API rejects the request citing a specific reasoning item ID (rs_...) that was generated in the previous turn. This suggests that the AI SDK or the OpenAI provider is maintaining state (perhaps via previous_response_id or similar mechanism) that links the new request to the previous reasoning steps, even when messages are stateless.

**3. Reasoning Summary**: We explicitly removed reasoningSummary from the provider options, but the issue persists.

### Hypothesis
The AI SDK's OpenAI provider, when detecting reasoningEffort, might be:

Automatically using the Responses API's stateful features (e.g., previous_response_id) without explicit opt-in.
Or, streamText is somehow retaining context from the previous turn if the same model instance is reused (though we create a new instance each time).

### Reproduction Steps

Setup:

AI SDK with OpenAI provider (currently using ai@5.0.47, @ai-sdk/openai@2.0.32)
Model enabled for reasoning (e.g., o1 or compatible).
reasoningEffort: "medium".

Scenario:

Turn 1: User asks a question that triggers a tool call.
Turn 1 Response: Model reasons (generating rs_... items internally) and calls a tool.
Turn 2: Tool result is fed back to the model.
Turn 2 Request: We send the history (User -> Assistant [Tool Call] -> Tool [Result]).
Result: 400 Bad Request: "Item 'rs_...' of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item."
Logs for Reference
Clean Input (verified):

```
[DEBUG] Sending messages to AI SDK: [
  {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": [
      { "type": "text", "text": "" },
      { "type": "tool-call", "toolCallId": "call_tjFuhKhDUrrDlJFwVEM3wrdc", ... }
    ]
  },
  {
    "role": "tool",
    "content": [
      { "type": "tool-result", "toolCallId": "call_tjFuhKhDUrrDlJFwVEM3wrdc", ... }
    ]
  }
]
```

Error:

`[ERROR] LLM Error: LLMRequestError - Item 'rs_0a1dc6172fd02e9d006922c262186881a2ab262138141fcf92' of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item.`

body:
No - but we can't know that. When you e.g. use an MCP toolset, you do not know what tools are in there. All tools that are created at runtime without static typing are considered dynamic tools. The tool calls and results contain both static and dynamic tools.

If you know you only have static tools, you can also use `.staticToolCalls` instead of `.toolCalls`.

body:
If you have been experiencing this, it's because you're using legacy tsconfig settings, namely `moduleResolution: "node"`. There's no reason to be using this anymore. The root cause was a very subtle resolution bug that caused both ESM and CJS versions of Zod to be loaded in the codebase simultaneously. TypeScript considers these independent constructs, resulting in  assignability issues and associated slow TS performance and occasionally OOM errors.

The simplest fix for this is to upgrade to a modern `moduleResolution` setting: https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#moduleResolution. The old `"node"` setting mirrored the behavior of Node 10 which hit EOL in 2021.

That said, I found a mitigation on Zod's end that also resolves this issue. Upgrade to `zod@4.1.6` and you won't hit this anymore: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/5222

body:
I found out why it happened, but not a proper fix with the Gemini 2.5 flash model.

The finishReason=error is an internal error code in this SDK and is mapped from the error message MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL sent by Gemini. That made debugging quite a bit easier and it turns out a lot of people are struggling with the same problem.

The condition I observed that resulted in this error was often large context and/or complex tool calls, which results in the Gemini model producing invalid JSON and the Gemini API returning the error code.

I read that some have had good effect by instructing the model to produce correct JSON during function calling, but that did not help my case.

I verified the assumption by running the 2.5 pro model where all my tests passed every time. 

My conclusion is that Google will probably not fix this issue and I’m better off waiting for a new Gemini model which will come end of this year.

But please feel free to share any other hacks fixing this issue!

body:
A single streaming response creates or adds to a single assistant message. Multiple assistant messages in a single stream are not supported by design in AI SDK 5. It breaks many assumptions that will cause issues in different parts of the system.

We may want to consider this in future release, so I will leave this open as a feature request.

Can you shed light on the use cases and how this would work with subsequent requests?
author: lgrammel

body:
I understand the potential concurrency issues (e.g., if there are multiple messages, determining which message should receive parts when there's no strict finish message part).

However, here's my use case: I'm building a multi-agent AI app that requires multi-stage responses with the following flow:

1. **Stream a first text result** - An orchestrator agent introduces the plan (as a message)
2. **Send progress notifications** - Worker agents send updates via transient events consumed through the `onData` callback
3. **Stream final result** - Final agent streams its text result in a separate "message" (which I expect to be distinct from the first one)

## Alternative Approaches I've Considered

### Text-start/text-end Level Approach
I considered working at the text-start/text-end level to display "chat bubbles" but this would require flattening `messages.parts`, which would prevent me from using "non-transient" data parts (or force me to use the hacky approach of sharing the text start ID in data parts and grouping parts by text start ID).

### Custom State Management Hack

body:
Hey I've been thinking about this a lot. I'd like to start with a question to @lgrammel. You say:

> A single streaming response creates or adds to a single assistant message. Multiple assistant messages in a single stream are not supported by design in AI SDK 5. It breaks many assumptions that will cause issues in different parts of the system.

Is there a chance to hear what exactly are those assumptions and why, "by design", the support was given up? The data representation of agent output is very "core" architectural decision and I think we should all understand how AI SDK team thinks about it and what's the framework direction.

I think it's possible to think of assistant `UIMessage` in 2 ways:
1. as a single call to the LLM (a full output of a single `streamText` call)
2. as a entire agent *run* output (*everything* that happens between user input and the final output of agent)

#### Assumption 1.

If we assume 1., then the points in this thread are very on point. The model breaks down pretty quickly:
- the agent "run" often consists of multiple LLM calls, for example in workflows (which are documented btw). Workflow steps absolutely can be persisted and displayed in the UI as separate items.
- in multi-agent systems handoffs literally a "primitive" (look at [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/handoffs/))

Having multiple multiple `streamText` calls in a a single agent run is so frequent that forcing just one `UIMessage` in output stream is extremely limiting. IMO, you shouldn't assume you can provide `streamText` abstraction **so good** that a single call to it handles all the use cases. It's gonna take very long time and imo it can end up with "abstraction hell" which made so many AI frameworks almost unusable (i.e. LLamaIndex or early LangChain).

Therefore, if we assume that assistant `UIMessage` is an output of a single `streamText` then multiple `UIMessage` are almost a must-have feature.

#### Assumption 2

We could think of assistant `UIMessage` as "entire run output". By "run output" I understand all the events that happened between user input to final assistant response - all LLM calls, workflows steps, agent hand-offs etc.

It means that with workflows or multi-agent systems, all the run output should be saved as `parts` of a single assistant `UIMessage`. That would imply that we always end up with data in format: `[user, assistant, user, assistant, ...]`, without *ever* having 2 consecutive assistant messages. 

That would require, in case of having multiple `streamText` calls, to "merge" the streams into a single response stream. And adding some glue code that can take ui messages and transform them into model messages properly case by case. But it's doable -> even today!

#### My take

Tbh I think Assumption 2 is pretty nice. But I don't know if this is a correct way of "thinking in ai-sdk". Imo it would require adding an explicit limitation that 2 consecutive assistant messages are not supported.

I like Assumption 2, because it makes the data format very clean. It's just user parts, assistant parts, user parts, etc... 

OpenAI pushed this even further. It uses a **plain array** without any message wrappers (!) to represent conversation history in Responses API. User message, assistant message, reasoning block, tool call blocks etc... all are represented as items in a single long array. Imo it's super clean and very powerful. And with Agents SDK they extended this way of thinking into multi-agent systems easily, it's still an array!

Very curious on your thoughts @lgrammel. Where are we going :-)

body: [DNA] [16:27:37] NeoGenesis: ## ⚡️ Résumé rapide Le problème vient du fait que **l’SDK AI inclut automatiquement un champ `logprobs` = 0** dans la requête OpenAI — ce qui fait que la réponse contient une matrice de `[]` pour chaque token. `generateText` n’inclut pas ce champ, d’où l’écart que vous observez. --- ## 🔍 Analyse technique | Élément | Observation | Cause probable | |---------|-------------|----------------| | `streamText` | `providerMetadata.openai.logprobs` → un tableau de centaines d’`[]` | Le SDK applique par défaut `logprobs: 0` si aucune valeur n’est fournie. | | `generateText` | `providerMetadata.openai.logprobs` absent | Le SDK ne requête pas `logprobs` pour l’appel “completion” (mode non‑stream). | | OpenAI API | Si `logprobs` est `0`, la réponse contient un tableau vide pour chaque token. | Même si vous ne l’avez pas explicitement demandé. | > **Conclusion** : le SDK ne respecte pas la *semantique* attendue (absence de champ `logprobs` quand vous ne l’avez pas demandé). > Cela a été signalé dans le tracker sous **#7951**. --- ## ✅ Solution immédiate ### 1️⃣ Spécifiez explicitement `logprobs: null` `null` indique à l’API OpenAI de ne pas renvoyer de logprobs du tout. ```ts import { generateText, streamText } from 'ai'; import 'dotenv/config'; import { openai, type OpenAIResponsesProviderOptions } from '@ai-sdk/openai'; async function main() { const options = { model: openai('gpt-4o-mini'), prompt: 'What is specifically notable about the style of Sonoran food?', providerOptions: { openai: { logprobs: null as unknown as number | null, // ← explicitement désactivé } satisfies OpenAIResponsesProviderOptions, }, }; const streamResult = await streamText(options); console.log( 'PROVIDER METADATA FORM STREAMTEXT:', JSON.stringify(await streamResult.providerMetadata, null, 2), ); const generateResult = await generateText(options); console.log( '\nPROVIDER METADATA FORM GENERATETEXT:', JSON.stringify(await generateResult.providerMetadata, null, 2), ); } main().catch(console.error); ``` > ⚠️ `as unknown as number | null` est uniquement là pour satisfaire le type TS. > Vous pouvez aussi omettre le type si votre TS‑config le permet. ### 2️⃣ Alternative : ne pas passer de `providerOptions` Si vous n’avez pas besoin d’autres options, retirez complètement l’objet `providerOptions`. Le SDK ne passera alors pas de champ `logprobs` du tout. ```ts const options = { model: openai('gpt-4o-mini'), prompt: 'What is specifically notable about the style of Sonoran food?', // providerOptions omitted → pas de logprobs }; ``` ### 3️⃣ Patch local (si vous ne voulez pas attendre la release) Si vous avez besoin d’une solution temporaire dans votre codebase, vous pouvez forcer le SDK à filtrer le champ `logprobs` avant de l’exposer : ```ts import { streamText } from 'ai'; import { sanitizeProviderMetadata } from '@ai-sdk/core'; // hypothétique utilité const streamResult = await streamText(options); const metadata = await streamResult.providerMetadata; // Suppression du champ logprobs si présent if (metadata.openai?.logprobs && Array.isArray(metadata.openai.logprobs)) { delete metadata.openai.logprobs; } console.log(JSON.stringify(metadata, null, 2)); ``` *(Cette fonction `sanitizeProviderMetadata` n’existe pas encore ; vous pouvez la créer vous‑même.)* --- ## 📌 Points clés à retenir | Point | Détails | |-------|---------| | **Cause** | `logprobs` par défaut = 0 dans l’SDK → tableau vide | | **Effet** | Métadonnées de `streamText` très volumineuses | | **Fix** | `logprobs: null` ou omettre `providerOptions` | | **À surveiller** | Issue #7951 → le bug est en cours de résolution dans le prochain patch de `@ai-sdk/core` | --- ## 🚀 Prochaine étape 1. **Appliquez l’un des correctifs ci‑dessus**. 2. **Vérifiez** que `streamText` renvoie maintenant : ```json { "openai": { "responseId": "resp_..." } } ``` 3. **Soumettez** un PR ou une issue sur le repo GitHub de l’AI SDK si vous pensez que la suppression du champ `logprobs` par défaut est un problème plus large. --- ### Remarque finale Si vous avez besoin de logprobs à l’avenir, vous pouvez toujours demander explicitement : ```ts openai: { logprobs: 5 } // ou tout autre nombre ``` et alors le champ apparaîtra avec les données attendues. En l’absence de cette option, il faut le désactiver explicitement comme montré ci‑dessus.

body:
Hi Ben, thanks for submitting the issue!

Just adding some more context while juggling other work.

- Docs on `instructions` argument: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses/create#responses_create-instructions
- Docs on `inputs[]`: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/text - interestingly, there is no `role: "system"` shown here, only `role: "developer"`
- We have an existing example to test the behavior end-to-end: [examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/openai-responses.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/1766edec300deb05c84bb7fefc034af4c2bc1165/examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/openai-responses.ts) which does log out the system message as part of `input` as reported by Ben

  ```
  input: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },
    { role: 'user', content: [Array] }
  ],
  ```

- We do remove the `role: 'system'` content from `response.messages`, which conforms with the behavior documented for `instructions`, it wouldn't break that behavior if we changed for using `input[0]` to `instructions` instead

- I tried to set both `system` and `providerOptions.openai.instructions` which did send a request with both the `instructions` property and `input[0].type === 'system'`. Interestingly, the system content in `input` took presedence over the `instructions` parameter.

- `providerOptions.openai.instructions` were added in #5385, which closed https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5274

body:
So what I ended up doing to get numbers that make sense:
- use `result.totalUsage` (instead of `result.usage`) to get most numbers (input, output, cache read).
- hook into `onStepFinish` and `extractStepCacheCreationInputTokens(step)` to get the cache creation tokens for each step and sum them up.

Where the function definition is:
```ts
function extractStepCacheCreationInputTokens({ providerMetadata }: ai.StepResult<any>): number {
  const anthropicUsage = providerMetadata?.anthropic?.usage as Record<string, number> | undefined;
  const anthropicCacheCreationTokens = anthropicUsage?.cache_creation_input_tokens;
  return typeof anthropicCacheCreationTokens === "number" ? anthropicCacheCreationTokens : 0;
}
```

The above gave me numbers that make sense.

Should be noted I did not extract 5m vs 1h cache tokens, as we're using only 5m on our end. You could extract it from the provider metadata.

Would be nice if the `ai` package would:
- Avoid the confusing `usage` vs `totalUsage` in `StreamTextResult`. it makes sense for a single step, not for the result of all steps.
- Provide me with the cache creation token counts for 5m vs 1h.
- Sum Anthropic's `providerMetadata` on `StreamTextResult` of multi-step flow. The provider should have done it. Having it equal to the result of the last step is weird.

Per [Anthropic's doc](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#tracking-cache-performance):

- `cache_creation_input_tokens`: Number of tokens written to the cache when creating a new entry.
- `cache_read_input_tokens`: Number of tokens retrieved from the cache for this request.
- `input_tokens`: Number of input tokens which were not read from or used to create a cache.

The input tokens from anthropic should be `cache_creation_input_tokens` + `input_tokens`. I'm not sure how we should track the fact that the cached input tokens are more expensive that non cached one, but all those are new input tokens.

### Identify issue type

**Identified type: Feature**  
Confidence: Medium

Rationale: The issue asks for added support/new capability for tool model output handling, not a documented current behavior failure.

author: lgrammel

body:
@lgrammel  I looked into this and wanted to lay out concrete use cases + the design tradeoff, since the unclear use case is the blocker 
## The gap
`createToolModelOutput` short-circuits on the error path and never calls a tool's `toModelOutput`. So when a tool call fails, the developer has no way to control how that failure is rendered to the model, it's always a generic `error-text` (`getErrorMessage`) or raw `error-json`. The return type already permits `error-text` / `error-json` parts; the hook just isn't invoked on errors.

## Use case 1: structured, recoverable errors

A tool hits a rate limit (429 with `Retry-After`). Today the model only sees a flat string. With the hook it gets a machine-readable signal it can act on (wait and retry, or tell the user):

    before: {"type":"error-text","value":"429 Too Many Requests"}
    after : {"type":"error-json","value":{
              "code":"rate_limited","retryAfterSeconds":5,
              "suggestion":"Wait retryAfterSeconds, then call the tool again."}}

## Use case 2: redact sensitive data before it leaves the process

Raw errors routinely leak connection strings, credentials, internal hostnames, PII, and stack traces  and today they go straight to the model *and* the provider. `toModelOutput` on the error path is the only place to sanitize at this layer:

    before: {"type":"error-text","value":"connection to postgres://admin:s3cr3t@10.0.0.4:5432/prod failed: password authentication failed for user 'admin'"}
    after : {"type":"error-text","value":"Database is temporarily unavailable."}

Other cases this unlocks: turning an opaque error into self-correction guidance ("date must be ISO-8601, you passed ..."), truncating huge upstream error bodies to control token cost, and normalizing every tool's error to one schema an agent is prompted to understand.

## Why the existing workaround isn't enough

The closest thing today is catching inside `execute` and returning a normal value (e.g. `return { ok: false, ... }`). But that turns the result into a `tool-result`, not a `tool-error` — so `steps.filter(p => p.type === 'tool-error')`, `onError`, and telemetry all stop seeing it as a failure. It also can't cover provider-executed tools or errors thrown outside `execute`. Handling this in `toModelOutput` keeps the `tool error` semantics intact while letting the developer shape the model-facing rendering. (`onError` only affects what's shown to the client, not the result fed back to the model; `experimental_repairToolCall` repairs inputs — neither applies here.

## Proposed API

Extend the existing hook with a second argument:

    toModelOutput(output, { error })

On the error path, `output` carries the error and `options.error === true`. Returning `undefined` falls back to the default rendering, so a tool can handle only the cases it cares about and leave the rest alone.

## One tradeoff worth deciding up front

There are two ways to do this:

1. **Second arg on `toModelOutput`** (above) : smallest surface, matches the issue title. Downside: an existing tool with an unguarded `toModelOutput` would now also run on errors (behavior change). The `undefined` fallback softens this but doesn't fully remove it.
2. **A separate `errorToModelOutput` hook** : fully additive, opt-in, zero behavior change. Slightly more API surface.

One thing to flag either way: the value passed on the error path isn't currently consistent across entry points (raw `Error` from `generateText`, a `getErrorMessage` string for provider-executed, `errorText` string from `convertToModelMessages`), so normalizing that would be part of the work.

I have a working prototype of option 1 (with the `undefined` fallback) and can open a PR - or go with option 2 if you'd prefer strictly non-breaking. Which direction do you want?

When using `gpt-oss-120b` with default gateway params I get:

```

result.text {"text":"A Shiba smiles with fox-like grace,\nCurled tail dancing, quick in pace.\nEyes that sparkle, sharp and sly,\nChasing breezes, under sky."}{"summary":"The poem depicts a lively Shiba dog, describing its fox-like smile, energetic tail, sparkling sharp eyes, and its playful, breezy nature."}
```

Notice that we have **two concatenated JSONs in the resulting text**. If you attempt to extract the `result.experimental_output` you get the familiar `AI_NoOutputSpecifiedError` error:
```
NoOutputSpecifiedError [AI_NoOutputSpecifiedError]: No output specified.
    at DefaultGenerateTextResult.get experimental_output (/Users/jeffrey/Projects/outnurture/node_modules/.pnpm/ai@5.0.82_zod@4.1.12/node_modules/ai/src/generate-text/generate-text.ts:843:13)
    at main (/Users/jeffrey/Projects/outnurture/.ignore/aisdk-exp-output-bug-og.ts:83:67)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:103:5) {
  cause: undefined,
  Symbol(vercel.ai.error): true,
  Symbol(vercel.ai.error.AI_NoOutputSpecifiedError): true
```

## the culprit(s)

Upon further inspection into `providerMetadata`, I found that some providers (_cerebras & groq_) 400 error when using tools and JSON mode. When failed this way, the gateway falls back to other providers. Unfortunately, some provider (_parasail, bedrock, baseten_) requests succeed but are consistently broken at agent runtime. There's only one provider that succeeds at generating the object: _fireworks_. 

Here's what the provider metadata looks like:

```json
providerMetadata {
  "gateway": {
    "routing": {
      "originalModelId": "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
      ...
      "attempts": [
        {
          "provider": "cerebras",
          "internalModelId": "cerebras:gpt-oss-120b",
          "success": false,
          "error": "\"tools\" is incompatible with \"response_format\"", // not allowed
          "statusCode": 400
        },
        {
          "provider": "groq",
          "internalModelId": "groq:openai/gpt-oss-120b",
          "success": false,
          "error": "json mode cannot be combined with tool/function calling", // not allowed
          "statusCode": 400
        },
        {
          "provider": "baseten",
          "internalModelId": "baseten:openai/gpt-oss-120b",
          "success": true, // success but will fail to generate parseable object.
          "statusCode": 200
        }
      ],
      ...
}
```

What this tells me is that **the ability to do JSON mode + tool calling with gpt-oss-120b  is determined at the provider-level**. I looked into the attempted results generated by each provider and found that they are each unique in their failures. For example, the _bedrock_ implementation generates the concatenated JSONs I mentioned at before.

## TL;DR 

✅ If you're using `gpt-oss-120b` and want to have `experimental_output` with tool calling then set your [provider options ](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/provider-options) to only use fireworks: 

```ts
  const providerOptions = {
    gateway: {
      order: [
        "cerebras", // 400 error --> fallback
        "groq", // 400 error --> fallback
        // "parasail", // 200 --> unsuccessfully generates object
        // "bedrock", // 200 --> unsuccessfully generates object
        // "baseten", // 200 --> unsuccessfully generates object
        "fireworks", // 200 --> successfully generates object 🎉
      ],
    },
  };
```

---

Smaller models like gpt-5-nano were generating args that exceeded schema limits, which led to invalid tool calls and then the “reasoning without following item” error. Example: the model returned 5 queries for a vector search while the schema caps it at 4. Preprocessing the args to clamp to the schema (or using a more capable model that respects constraints) eliminated the issue entirely.

Hi all, apologies for the delay! 

Reusable prompts would be a major change and as of now it's out of scope for the AI SDK. Our base assumption that everything else is built around the messages we send to providers, how we handle their response and multi-turn request/response cycles. The feature is also OpenAI-specific, we have to wait and see if other providers implement similar functionality, at which point we can consider to update our spec. Changing the spec is always a breaking change.

I double checked to make sure we send the right arguments with your provided example (I updated [this one](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/0a87932a297ea225034a489664b0d53ef0c52333/examples/ai-core/src/transcribe/openai-string.ts) for testing).

Here is what we send

```
FormData {
  model: 'whisper-1',
  file: File {
    size: 882477,
    type: 'audio/mpeg',
    name: 'audio',
    lastModified: 1757016823557
  },
  response_format: 'verbose_json',
  temperature: '0',
  timestamp_granularities: 'word'
}
```

Which is not quite correct. `timestamp_granularities` accepts an array, it should be

```
FormData {

  'timestamp_granularities[]': 'word'
}
```

Hi! I've read through the discussion and see @codybrouwers' excellent analysis and patch.

I'd like to implement this as a proper PR. The fix uses the local variable capture pattern in the finally block - a well-established practice for handling this type of race condition.

My plan:
1. Declare `let activeResponse` before try block
2. Assign to local var first, then to `this.activeResponse`
3. Use local var in finally block with null check
4. Add test case for the error scenario
5. Add patch changeset

Thanks to @codybrouwers for identifying the root cause and providing the solution. I'll submit a PR shortly.

body:
Hi @abhi-slash-git, thanks for the excellent bug report and clear reproduction case.

 @gr2m, I've completed a deep dive and can confirm the root cause. The message conversion logic wasn't correctly ordering tool_result parts before user text and had some inconsistencies in handling mixed assistant content, which violates Anthropic's strict message sequence requirements.

I have a fix ready in PR #8524

The PR normalizes the message structure to solve this. It also includes comprehensive tests covering your exact scenario, plus several other edge cases to prevent future regressions.

As a side note, I also discovered a separate, more subtle bug where provider-executed tools (like web_search) lose their special typing when sent as role: "tool". To keep this PR focused, I have opened a new, dedicated issue to track that here #8527

body:
We're hitting a related issue but with a slightly different error message.

## Environment

- ai: 6.0.0-beta.126
- @ai-sdk/gateway: 2.0.0-beta.68
- @ai-sdk/openai: 3.0.0-beta.74
- Next.js 15.6.0-canary.58

## Error

```
TypeError: t.content is not iterable
    at ... (AI SDK internal stream processing)
    → AI_NoOutputGeneratedError
    → ResponseAborted
```

## Setup

We have a multi-agent system using `streamText()` with tool calls. Messages are persisted to PostgreSQL and rehydrated on subsequent requests.

Our message flow:
1. Load messages from DB
2. Convert DB format to ModelMessage format
3. Validate tool-call/tool-result pairs (remove orphans)
4. Pass to `streamText()` with Anthropic models (Claude Sonnet 4.5)

We use Anthropic prompt caching with the array format:
```ts
system: isAnthropicModel ? [
  {
    type: 'text',
    text: systemPrompt,
    providerOptions: {
      anthropic: { cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' } }
    }
  }
] : systemPrompt
```

## What we already do

1. Validate message sequences - ensure every `tool-call` is immediately followed by its `tool-result`
2. Use microsecond offsets on timestamps to guarantee DB ordering
3. Filter out orphaned tool messages before passing to SDK

## Observations

The crash happens intermittently, not on every request. It seems related to:
- Longer conversations with multiple tool calls
- Parallel tool execution (multiple tool calls in one step)

The error occurs inside the SDK's stream processing, not at the Anthropic API level.

## Current workaround

We're implementing automatic fallback to OpenAI models when this error occurs with Anthropic.

---

Would be helpful to know if PR #10742 addresses this specific variation of the issue.

body: I think I found the solution. The issue happens because the `step-start` part is missing. Here is what the response from Anthropic looks like with a single tool call. Note the `step-start` _after_ the tool call. If you check the [relevant part](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/b36806328095e3026e167b52ce671c4861bdb496/packages/ai/src/ui/convert-to-model-messages.ts#L338) in the source code, you will see a call to `processBlock()`. This function handles the addition of `tool-result` blocks in the case of tools calls. However, this is only executed if the `step-start` block is present when iterating over the parts. In the case of Anthropic, their API is probably very adamant about the existence of the `tool_result` block, while other APIs are less strict. I have struggled with this issue for months, and this fix solved it for good. I was filtering `step-start` parts in my code because I thought they aren't needed. Turns out they are. Hope this will also fix the issue for others as I haven't seen this solution mentioned by anyone else yet.

Rationale: The issue reports a concrete incorrect current behavior in the SDK's Anthropic message rehydration path: provider-executed tool result type information is lost across turns. Although fixes are suggested, the primary claim is a broken behavior affecting existing multi-turn usage.

body:
For what it's worth. Claude found a simple workaround for this.

```ts
const steps = await streamResult.steps;
const allToolCalls = steps.flatMap((step) => step.toolCalls);
```

Here's the full explanation for context, and hopefully to aid in fixing this issue:

> I found it. Look at line 5999-6000:
> 
> ```javascript
> if (part.type === "start-step") {
>   recordedContent = [];  // <-- Content is RESET for each step!
> ```
> 
> And then look at how `toolCalls` is resolved (line 6792-6793):
> 
> ```javascript
> get toolCalls() {
>   return this.finalStep.then((step) => step.toolCalls);
> }
> ```
> 
> **The issue**: `toolCalls` returns `finalStep.toolCalls` - the tool calls from the **LAST** step only.
> 
> Looking at your `messages` data, there are **3 steps**:
> 1. **Step 1**: Assistant with reasoning + text + `tool-call`
> 2. **Step 2**: Tool role with `tool-result` 
> 3. **Step 3**: Assistant with final text
> 
> The `finalStep` is Step 3 - which has no tool calls, just the final text response. The tool calls are in Step 1, but `toolCalls` only looks at the last step!
> 
> Let me verify by checking if there's a way to get all steps:
> 
> [1 tool called]
> 
> **Root cause confirmed**: `streamResult.toolCalls` returns `finalStep.toolCalls` - only the **last step's** tool calls, not all tool calls across the entire multi-step generation.
> 
> Your flow has 3 steps.
> 
> The SDK provides `streamResult.steps` to access all steps. The proper fix:
> 
> [2 tools called]
> 
> The fix uses `streamResult.steps` to get all steps, then extracts tool calls from each step with `steps.flatMap((step) => step.toolCalls)`.
> 
> **Summary of the issue**:
> - The AI SDK's `streamResult.toolCalls` only returns tool calls from `finalStep` (the last step)
> - In multi-step tool execution, the tool calls happen in earlier steps, not the final one
> - The final step is just the text response after tool execution, which has no tool calls
> - Using `streamResult.steps` gives access to all steps, allowing you to collect tool calls from the entire conversation

body: Why do you need tools with a `never` input or output? it does not make sense in the ai sdk since tools will always get called and have an input and also always produce some sort of output that is sent back to the llm
author: lgrammel

body:
@lgrammel I think there are use cases for tools which either take no input (those that return some fact or current state - e.g. "what is the current time") or which return no output (those which instruct an action but where the LLM does not need the result to continue e.g. "remember this fact about the user").

That being said, it's a totally valid architectural choice to say "no, the ai SDK always requires an input and output for a Tool" but then the defect here is that the type signature for `Tool` and `ToolSet` both explicitly allow input or output to be `never` (well, ToolSet **partially** allows that...). If we want to prohibit never input/output, then those signatures should be updated to make that clearer earlier in the chain.

body:
The use cases that you are mention are already supported:

a) for inputs LLMs usually send an empty object
b) for outputs I agree (since we now have toModelOutput) it could be useful but would prefer the type to be void or undefined vs never

> About the "bug", reading the code, I see everything totally normal

> `runToolsTransformation` receives all tools because it's not responsible for deciding which tool is called. The model generates a tool-call chunk, and runToolsTransformation just intercepts that call

Yes, that is correct.

The issue is inside the callstack of `runToolsTransformation`.

It uses this code:

```ts
const { toolChoice: stepToolChoice, tools: stepTools } =
            prepareToolsAndToolChoice({
              tools,
              toolChoice: prepareStepResult?.toolChoice ?? toolChoice,
              activeTools: prepareStepResult?.activeTools ?? activeTools,
            });
```

to filter `tools` down to `stepTools` based on `activeTools`, but then a couple lines later it does:

`doParseToolCall(tools)`, instead of `doParseToolCall(stepTools)` (that is the bug, IMO).

body:
[Some initial research with ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/share/68d0c70d-eb20-8011-8e16-11543e995200)

### Feature support

Legend: ✅ = supported natively; 🟨 = supported via specific hosted model(s)/partial; — = not evident.

| Provider | Outpaint | Inpaint | Upscale | Variations | Restyle (img2img) | Masked/Local Restyle | Background Remove | Notes / Docs |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| **amazon-bedrock** | ✅ | ✅ | 🟨 | 🟨 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Titan Image + partner models. |
| **deepinfra** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Model hub (Bria/Qwen/FLUX, etc.); capability varies by model. |
| **fal** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 🟨 | ✅ | ✅ | 🟨 | Endpoints for inpaint/outpaint/upscalers; “Kontext” for local edits. |
| **fireworks** | 🟨 | 🟨 | — | 🟨 | ✅ | ✅ | — | FLUX models; “Kontext” supports local edits. |
| **google-vertex** | ✅ | ✅ | 🟨 | 🟨 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Imagen on Vertex: mask/reference editing; background ops available. |
| **openai** | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | Images API: edits (mask), variations (DALL·E-style), img2img via edits. |
| **replicate** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Wide model catalog (inpaint/outpaint/upscale/rmbg/instruct-pix2pix). |
| **togetherai** | 🟨 | 🟨 | — | 🟨 | ✅ | ✅ | — | FLUX models with in-context/local edit behavior. |

### Common variables

#### Inpainting (masked edits)
- `image` / `image_url`, `mask` / `mask_image` (binary/alpha)
- `prompt`, optional `negative_prompt`
- Strength/conditioning: `strength`, `guidance_scale`, `num_inference_steps`, `seed`
- Output size: `width`/`height` or `size`/`aspect_ratio`

#### Outpainting (canvas expansion)
- `image`
- `prompt`
- Canvas/region: `expand`/`outpaint_mode`/`new_size` (or supply a border mask)
- Usual sampler fields: `steps`, `guidance`, `seed`

#### Upscaling / Super-resolution
- `image` / `image_url`
- Scale factor: `scale` (e.g., 2×, 4×)
- Quality options: `tile`, `face_enhance`, `sharpen`

#### Image variations
- `image`, optional `prompt` to steer
- Variation intensity: `variation_strength`/`strength`
- Sampling: `num_inference_steps`, `guidance_scale`, `seed`, `n` (count)

#### Restyle (img2img)
- `image`
- `prompt` (target style)
- Deviation control: `strength` (how far from source), `guidance_scale`, `steps`, `seed`

#### Masked/Local restyle
- **Masked**: same as Inpainting + style-oriented `prompt`
- **Local (mask-less)**: `image` + natural-language region (“make the shirt yellow”); size/aspect optional

#### Background remove/replace
- `image`
- Output mode: transparent alpha vs composited
- Optional replacement: `prompt` or `background_image`

### Notes & caveats

- **Aggregators vs. single-vendor APIs**: Replicate, DeepInfra, fal, Fireworks, Together host many models; support depends on the specific model chosen.  
- **Mask vs. “local edits”**: Some modern editors target regions via text prompts instead of hard masks; still effectively “masked restyle.”  
- **Upscaling**: Dedicated SR models (e.g., ESRGAN variants) generally outperform “just request a larger size” in gen-models.

body:
I'm not sure using Anthropic as the comparison is the best choice, from what I've seen it is Anthropic with the non-consensus behavior, as OpenAI/Gemini/other providers all provide "input tokens" as the total count of input tokens, and then provide "cached input tokens" as the number of those input tokens that were a cache hit.

However I do agree with you that ideally the AI-sdk would be opinionated in the definition/consistency of these fields, as I have to special case the Anthropic behavior (both via the Anthropic provider as well as Claude on Vertex) in my codebase to do cost estimates.
author: danielamitay

body:
Agree @danielamitay, they are in large the odd one out - also agree that the biggest impact here would be to have an opinionated definition of what the fields are.

I'm sure you've already noticed, it appears all providers have slightly non-consensus behavior making billing/ usage extremely tough. For example Gemini "output" tokens don't appear to include reasoning tokens when OAI "output" tokens do.

Gemini Usage
```javascript
{
  inputTokens: 2414,
  outputTokens: 120,
  totalTokens: 2699,
  reasoningTokens: 165,
  cachedInputTokens: 2025
}
```

OpenAI Usage
```javascript
{
  inputTokens: 2222,
  outputTokens: 658,
  totalTokens: 2880,
  reasoningTokens: 384,
  cachedInputTokens: 2048
}
```

Rather than debate which provider is closest to standard, I’d love to align on a DX-first schema that disentangles the combined fields into a set of mutually exclusive parts - then has some derived totals on-top (totalTokens, totalInputTokens, totalOutputTokens, ...) so it’s unambiguous.

Happy to spend some time and make a PR if that is of interest to the AI-SDK owners.

This avoids the error for now, so sharing in case it helps anyone else. ```ts export const handleExceptionOnOpenAi = ( message: UIMessage, ) => { // remove reasoning part if openai request is aborted // issue: https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8811 // "Item with id ... not found" error happens when the reasoning part is not removed. for (const part of message.parts) { if ( (part.type === 'reasoning' || part.type === 'text') && part.providerMetadata?.openai ) { part.providerMetadata = undefined; } } return message; }; // pesuedo code // update chat.messages manually import { Chat } from '@ai-sdk/react'; const chat = new Chat({ id, transport, messages, onData: data => { this.onData$.next(data); }, onFinish: {message, error, isAborted} => { if (isAborted) { const newMessage = handleExceptionOnOpenAi(message); replace(chat.message, newMessage); } }, onError: error => { this.onError$.next(error); }, }); ```

body:
While it looks like this is now documented in the migration guide, I have to say that non-strict output seems like a questionable default as someone who recently migrated from using the `openai` SDK directly. Because of that, I never looked at v4->v5 migration guides and so wouldn't have possibly seen this, and https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/generating-structured-data makes no mention of the fact that generation is _not_ strict by default. This caused issues in production, as now the model would sometimes randomly omit properties, which in turn would result in errors like these:

```
AI_NoObjectGeneratedError: No object generated: response did not match schema.
```

From reading #4662, I can _sort of_ understand why this change was made, but it's definitely confusing coming from `openai` where you'd have to jump through hoops to get it to not use strict mode when providing a Zod schema.

I think it'd be a great improvement to specifically call out on the "generating structured data" docs that it's necessary to configure individual providers to enable strict structured outputs.

body: The issue was not caused by the difference between generateText and streamText. The root cause was the parallel execution of generateText for multiple samples. A similar issue has been reported here: https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/5414
author: ehsan-eigen

body:
The follow-up in this thread points to the sharper failure mode: parallel calls, not `generateText` vs `streamText` by itself.

From current `main`, the OTel integration already has the right shape for single-call nesting: `OpenTelemetry` keeps `callStates` by `callId`, starts tool spans from the call's `stepContext`, stores them in `toolSpans`, and `executeTool` re-enters that tool span context before running the tool. The existing test that `chat` and `execute_tool` share the same step context is useful, but it only proves the single-call case.

The regression I would add is a concurrent one:

- start two or three `generateText`/`generateObject` calls with telemetry enabled and distinct `functionId`/trace metadata
- force their model/tool execution to interleave with resolvable promises
- assert every `execute_tool`/provider child span has the parent context for its own `callId`, not whichever call happened to be active first
- assert the exported trace/name/metadata for each parent remains distinct after all promises settle

That catches the exact class of bug people are seeing in Langfuse: the span exists, but the parent/name/metadata belong to another parallel invocation. The existing parallel `doEmbed` test is close in spirit, but this needs to cover the generate path plus tool/provider child spans.

---

Hi @lgrammel, thanks for your reply.

I have tried `readUIMessageStream` which is suitable for most cases, but `readUIMessageStream ` is always reading stream from start and performing structured clones on message object.

When I'm reading large and long duration streams with many steps and heavy tool calls:
-  structured clone costs cost too much (e.g. when I read from 100 chunks, 100 shadow clones executed but I only needs the last UIMessage object.)
-  it is not possible to handle reconnect scenario: intermediate streaming state (aka StreamingUIMessageState) is not exposed from `readUIMessageStream`

---
EDIT: shadow clone -> structured clone
We also have a similar need to access processUIMessageStream so we can create our own wrapper to handle multiple messages inside a single stream and manage multiple message states.

@aayush-kapoor 
> raised a pr, but when i ran the command `pnpm prettier-fix` there was around 3k file changes what should i do should i discard it and move on or push it in this pr

Hey, just in case you didn’t know — a quick info before you panic like I did the first time after running prettier:

Seeing lots of changes after running Prettier can be a bit irritating, but it’s actually a common thing on windows. Git doesn’t normalize things like line endings until you stage the files, so the diff before staging often looks much larger than it really is. Once you stage the files, most (or all) of those changes disappear.

A simple workaround: after running Prettier, stage all files once and then unstage them again. That way you’ll see the actual changes that matter.

body:
This is an interesting edge case. As @gr2m mentioned, this seems to happen when `activeTools` changes mid-conversation — the model retains a 'memory' of previously available tools and tries to call them even after they've been deactivated. The error message then dumps the full tool list instead of respecting the current `activeTools` filter.

The XML-like tool name in @MrRoiz's error (`tool1" />\n<invoke name="tool2" />\n<invoke name="tool3" />`) is particularly revealing — the model is literally pasting XML tool-call syntax as a tool name. This is a different failure mode than a simple wrong-tool-name hallucination; it looks like the model is confusing the tool call format with the tool name field.

For anyone hitting this in production, a pragmatic workaround is to catch the `NoSuchToolError` (or equivalent) in your middleware and either: (1) respond with a message telling the model which tools are currently active, or (2) silently retry the request with a system reminder. The former is more transparent; the latter is smoother UX.

We see this class of hallucination frequently — models confusing API formats, mangling tool names, or injecting markup into structured fields. It's one of the categories [open-code-review](https://github.com/raye-deng/open-code-review) checks for when reviewing AI-generated integration code.

I'm experiencing the same issue with the latest versions. The `@vercel/oidc@3.0.2` package is installed, but Metro is still trying to resolve the Node.js-only version instead of the browser-compatible export.

Error:
```
Unable to resolve "@vercel/oidc" from "node_modules/@ai-sdk/gateway/dist/index.js"
Metro has encountered an error: While trying to resolve module @vercel/oidc from file
/path/to/node_modules/@ai-sdk/gateway/dist/index.js, the package
[package.json](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) was successfully found. However, this package itself specifies a main module
field that could not be resolved (/path/to/node_modules/@vercel/oidc/index).
```

Versions installed: 
```json
    "@ai-sdk/openai": "^2.0.50",
"@ai-sdk/react": "^2.0.68",
"ai": "^5.0.68",
"expo": "~52.0.46"
```

Metro config (as suggested in the thread):

```
const { getSentryExpoConfig } = require('@sentry/react-native/metro')

const config = getSentryExpoConfig(__dirname)

config.resolver.unstable_enablePackageExports = true

config.resolver.unstable_conditionNames = [
  'browser',
  'react-native',
  'import',
  'require',
  'default',
]

module.exports = config
```

The @vercel/oidc@3.0.2 [package.json](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) does have the correct conditional exports:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "browser": "./dist/index-browser.js",
    "react-native": "./dist/index-browser.js",
    "import": "./dist/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/index.js"
  }
}
```

What I've tried:

- Set unstable_enablePackageExports: true
- Set unstable_conditionNames with browser and react-native first
- Updated to latest AI SDK versions
- Cleared all caches (rm -rf node_modules [yarn.lock](http://_vscodecontentref_/2) $TMPDIR/metro-* $TMPDIR/react-*)
- Clean rebuild (npx expo prebuild --clean)
- Verified the package exports exist in [package.json](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)

The issue persists on both iOS and Android, confirming it's a Metro bundling issue.

Despite having the correct Metro configuration and the package having the proper conditional exports, Metro is still attempting to resolve the Node.js version (index.js) instead of the browser/React Native version (index-browser.js).

Is there something specific about how @ai-sdk/gateway imports @vercel/oidc that bypasses the conditional exports? Or is there an issue with Metro's unstable_enablePackageExports feature in Expo SDK 52?

@gr2m  Any additional insights would be greatly appreciated!

I find the solution.

Safari has printed error
> Failed to load resource: Request header field User-Agent is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers.

So we just need to append the "User-Agent"  to server responses.
author: oboard

body:
> Is your server throwing the error? If so, I would add `User-Agent` to `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`

No, the error is in Safari. But I think what you're saying is correct. The browser does a preflight request that gets the allowed headers. In the actual request, Chrome overrides the custom header in order for it to be safelisted despite the server not sending User-Agent as an allowed header. Safari doesn't override and uses the custom `ai` header which causes it to fail. I imagine adding User-Agent to Access-Control-Allow-Headers would fix the problem so that I don't have to delete the header, but I can't do that currently

@lgrammel I would also love to understand why you decided to validate schema of input args on provider executed tool calls. I don't see many benefits of doing so, especially if the provider already does that for us from their end. I'd rather let the provider deal with that since it's a provider executed tool call; I think it's polluting the API with noise.

author: philiparpin

body:
Look at the timing:

DNS: Works fine -- resolves to 64.239.123.129 and 64.239.109.129 (Vercel's edge IPs via Cloudflare). No IPv6 issues.
TLS: ECONNRESET in 36ms
36ms is the smoking gun. That's not a timeout or a network issue -- that's an active rejection. The TCP connection succeeds (SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK), then Render sends the TLS ClientHello, and Vercel's edge immediately sends back a TCP RST. The connection is being deliberately killed.

Vercel's edge (Cloudflare) is looking at the source IP from Render and resetting the connection before TLS negotiation completes. A real network problem would timeout (seconds), not reset in 36ms. A TLS version mismatch would send a TLS alert, not a raw TCP RST.

So to directly answer your question -- the gateway itself is fine. It never even sees your requests. Cloudflare, sitting in front of Vercel's edge, is dropping connections from Render's IP range at the TCP layer. Whether that's intentional policy or collateral damage from abuse on shared Render IPs, only Vercel/Cloudflare can tell you.

Going direct to api.anthropic.com works because Anthropic's infrastructure doesn't have the same IP-level blocking.

body:
The onError approach of returning a string doesn't work for NoSuchToolError in our case. We're using streamText with experimental_repairToolCall, and here's what we found by reading the SDK source (
index.mjs
):

NoSuchToolError is caught internally by the SDK's parseToolCall function before it ever reaches onError.
The SDK first tries experimental_repairToolCall. If that returns null, it re-throws the original error, which is then caught by an outer try/catch that silently converts it into a dynamic: true tool call with no execute function — the error never propagates to onError.
Returning a string from onError doesn't actually inject that string as a tool result back into the conversation. The onError callback is a notification hook, not a recovery mechanism — its return value is ignored by the SDK.
So the flow is: NoSuchToolError → experimental_repairToolCall → if null → re-throw → outer catch creates dynamic tool call → stream continues without error reaching onError.

Could you clarify which AI SDK version and which specific streamText/generateText configuration you're using where returning a string from onError actually works? In our testing with AI SDK 5.x, the string return from onError has no effect on the conversation flow for NoSuchToolError.

The only reliable way we found to handle this is inside experimental_repairToolCall itself — returning a corrected toolCall object with a valid toolName that exists in the tools regis

body:
@JureSotosek 

I worked around the issue by implementing my own abort-signal system using **unstorage**, which comes with Nitro.

When I start a generation, I send a unique ID and store it in unstorage. The backend watches this key. I also created a separate route that, when called with the same ID, updates the key to an “abort” state.

Inside the generation loop, I check this key, and if it switches to “abort”, I stop the generation manually.

So basically I built my own abort mechanism using unstorage. It’s not ideal, but it works reliably with Nitro until proper abort propagation is fixed in the SDK.

**Root cause:** The Google provider was not calling `asSchema().jsonSchema` to extract the JSON Schema from `tool.inputSchema`, which is a `FlexibleSchema` type. This resulted in passing a Schema object (with a `jsonSchema` getter) instead of a plain JSONSchema7 object.

**Pull request:** #9762

The fix properly extracts the JSON schema using `await asSchema(tool.inputSchema).jsonSchema`, matching the pattern used in other parts of the codebase.

body:
Hey! The AI SDK's built-in agent loop mechanism is a tool-calling loop and is therefore built on the assumption that the model generating text (not a tool call) marks the end of the loop. The agent generating text either indicates it is done or it needs more information to proceed - the latter you can attempt to prompt away.

With that being said, you can build your own agent loop that builds on different assumptions. We'll be shipping more complex examples that showcase this pattern but, for now, check out this recipe: https://ai-sdk.dev/cookbook/node/manual-agent-loop.

body:
## Community Meeting from November 13, 2025

Notes from yesterdays call with @jephal, @tommasoghisini, and @rahulbhadja 

### Intros

- Jeppe and Tommaso are coworkers at [falck.com](https://www.falck.com/). They use the AI SDK and the Azure Provider for an internal chat app.
- Rahul is Co-founder of a startup using AI SDK with Azure-hosted models

### Learnings

- Azure is significantly different from other providers, making it complex to set up and debug
- Azure frequently changes naming conventions and repackages their AI services
- Content filtering and API versioning present additional challenges

### Priorities

- Code Interpreter File Downloads: Users can't easily download files generated by the Code Interpreter tool. We have an open pull request by @tsuzaki430 that needs to be updated: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/9135
- Telemetry Issues: 
  - short term: fix discrepancy between deployment ID and model ID in observability logs
  - longer term: observability will be a priority for the AI SDK soon, we will incorporate requirements by Azure
- Documentation is out of date since `azure.responses` was made the default: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/10209

### Next

- Azure Deep Research Integration: @tommasoghisini is exploring Azure's deep research setup with GPT-5 and grounding with Bing and will document findings to gauge community interest
- Interest in real-time models for live interactions, but these are not yet prioritized by AI SDK

Hello. The meeting is coming up soon , tomorrow!😊
I’m sorry that I won’t be able to attend, but instead I’d like to share my next goals.

* **Start working on the “Future Work” once PR #10266 is closed**
  This PR does not yet include documentation updates. There are several items to address, but I’d like to start by adding documentation.

* **Add CodeInterpreter file upload support to `examples/next-openai`**

  This applies to both `@ai-sdk/openai` and `@ai-sdk/azure`.

* **Recreate fixtures for Azure Responses API tests**
  I noticed that the `finishReason` in `azure-openai-provider.test.ts.snap` is ending up as `error`.
  At the time, I wasn’t aware of the `saveRawChunks` function, so I’d like to regenerate the fixtures and replace them with ones that complete through a more natural flow.

* **Add support for built-in tools in the Azure Responses API**
  Tools such as `mcp`, `shell`, and `apply_patch` may need to be added.
  `local_shell` may not need to be explicitly supported.

sure, the repo given by @gabimoncha show this -

V5 (main branch):
- "generateText()" with experimental_output + "tools" fails for:
  - **error/failss**- Groq: "json mode cannot be combined with "tool/function calling"
  - **error/fails**- Google: "Forced function calling (ANY mode) with a response mime type: 'application/json' is unsupported"
  - **doest work properly**- OpenRouter: Doesn't error but returns text instead of the structured object

- "generateObject()" works fine for all three providers when there aree no tools

V6 (ai-sdk-v6 branch):
- Same issues persist with "generateText({ output })"
- Additionally, "ToolLoopAgent" with "output" parameter:
  - **same erro/fails**- Groq/Google: Same errors as above
  - **doesnt fail but doesnt work properly**- OpenRouter: Stops after first tool call instead of continuing
  - **error/fails**- AI Gateway: Loops unnecessarily and fails to match schema

main issue:
When `output` (structured output) is combined with `tools`, the AI SDK core sends both responseFormat: { type: 'json', schema }` and `tools: [...]` to the provider. Providers like Groq and Google don't support this combination and reject it outright. 

this repo though documents that providers have different capabilities and the current AI SDK doesn't abstract these differences properly when combining structured output with tool calling. The fix needs to happen in at **ai-sdk/groq**, at **ai-sdk/google**, and at **openrouter/ai-sdk-provider** packages, not in the core as @gr2m you have mentioned it in closed PR review that i did.in
