body:
@nicoalbanese thanks for looking in the issue.

**Update: Root cause found and resolved**

Turns out my OpenAI API key had run out of quota. Once I replaced it with a valid key, streaming started working immediately.

The tricky part was that the AI SDK was silently swallowing the quota error - `streamText()` just returned an empty stream (0 chunks) without throwing any errors or triggering the `onError` callback. This made it really hard to debug since there was no indication anything was wrong.

I was already using `convertToModelMessages` and added `onError` as suggested, but the error was happening at a layer where those don't catch it. A direct fetch to OpenAI's API revealed the 429 quota error.

Now everything works great - middleware generates consistent cache keys and I'm seeing 26-69% faster TTFT on cached requests.

Might be worth considering surfacing API errors (quota, auth, etc.) more explicitly rather than silently failing, as it would make debugging much easier.

Hey! I was hoping to tackle some of these providers, and went through their API documentation to see how they expose usage information.

Outside of OpenAI's API, I couldn't find token usage data in the image generation APIs for any of the following endpoints:
- [``fal``](https://docs.fal.ai/model-apis/model-endpoints/synchronous-requests)

- [``luma``](https://docs.lumalabs.ai/docs/image-generation)
- [``replicate``](https://replicate.com/docs/reference/http#predictions.get-description)
- [``togetherai``](https://docs.together.ai/reference/post-images-generations)
- [``xai``](https://docs.x.ai/docs/api-reference#image-generations)

For [``amazon-bedrock``](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_CountTokens.html), I could  only find the ``CountTokens`` endpoint which wouldn't make sense to use. Some, like deepinfra, follow the OpenAI API Schema, but I don't believe they provide the usage token metadata regardless. It might be worth running inference to confirm that.

I've linked the documentation pages I referred to for each provider, in case you are able to find something I missed.

body:
Great report. The root cause is a classic LLM hallucination pattern where the model injects special characters (`$`) into tool names. The Bedrock API validates tool names against `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+` server-side, so the request crashes before `experimental_repairToolCall` can even intercept it — the validation happens at the API gateway level, not in the SDK.

We've seen similar patterns across providers: Claude tends to hallucinate ``, GPT models sometimes generate `<tool_name>` with angle brackets, and Gemini occasionally prepends `tools/`. It seems to correlate with how the model internalizes the tool schema — special characters in the schema definition or nearby tokens leak into the generated tool name.

A defensive fix would be to sanitize the `toolUse.name` field in the Bedrock adapter before sending it back to the API (strip non-alphanumeric characters), or to catch the validation error and retry with the cleaned name. This would let `experimental_repairToolCall` work as intended.

We built [open-code-review](https://github.com/raye-deng/open-code-review) partly to catch these kinds of AI hallucination patterns in code — tool name mangling, invented API endpoints, and fabricated package names are some of the most common categories.

body:
This is a bit of a tangent, but I’ve been looking into `annotations` and wanted to share my observations.

### url_citation

When the main content is Markdown, `streamDown` already converts URLs into links, so `url_citation` doesn’t feel strictly necessary for basic linking.  
Also, since we already have examples that use the AI Element “Source” view, we don’t really need `url_citation` just to build a list of links at the end of the message.

That said, there’s still room to make use of it—for example, to highlight URLs more prominently in the text, or to show tooltips with titles or source information.

### file_citation

At the moment, I find `file_citation` quite difficult to work with.

- Because `start_index` and `end_index` are not present, we can’t highlight “which part of the text came from which file” in the UI.
- The `index` property is, as far as I can tell, likely the index of a vectorized file chunk. However, I haven’t found any way to use that index to retrieve the corresponding text, so it’s hard to find a practical use for it.

I had been dreaming of building a nice “citation UI” for `file_search`, but with the current specification it’s very hard to achieve that. I honestly feel this is a bit of a missed opportunity.

### container_file_citation

Without converting `container_file_citation`, the text can end up containing paths that only make sense if you know what’s inside the container, which makes the content hard to understand for users.  
From a UX perspective, I think some kind of transformation is essentially required here.

In the AI SDK, we’re able to generate clickable download links from this annotation, so users can just click to open the file. I’m very happy with this UX.

### file_path

I haven’t actually used this one yet.  
I’m not sure what kind of prompt is needed to get this annotation to appear, so I haven’t been able to reliably reproduce its behavior.

My current guess is that it can be used to reference files that are not tied to a specific `containerId`.

Even if we figure out how to use `file_path`, I expect there will still be some uncertainty, since the properties don’t include fields like `filename` or `start_index`.


### Summary

Right now, `container_file_citation` feels like the most practically useful annotation.  
For the others, I think we would need additional API support or some careful UX design to make them truly useful in real-world applications.

Also, since `code_interpreter`’s `tool_result` does not include a `fileId`, extracting `fileId` from `container_file_citation` currently feels like a necessary step in the processing pipeline.

body:
> Gemini 3 models require a `thoughtSignature` on every `functionCall` part when replaying conversation history. The AI SDK normally preserves this through `callProviderMetadata`, but it's possible in certain edge cases for clients not to store/send it back. In our codebase, it can happen with client-side tool execution.
> 
> Google documents that `"skip_thought_signature_validator"` can be used as a dummy value when injecting function call blocks that weren't received from the model.
> 
> See https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures
> 
> As a workaround, you can inject the dummy signature into `callProviderMetadata` on any replayed tool-call parts that are missing the original signature:
> 
> const callProviderMetadata = {
>   google: { thoughtSignature: 'skip_thought_signature_validator' }
> };

I did that, but I still have issue when agents need to hand off work to another agent. It just break and stop.

body:
@nicoalbanese 
I have already implemented the changes to the project , was just adding the test cases before making the pr.

Reading through the doc i found that anthropic expects request body to contain a context_management object with this structure:

**Tool_use:**

```
    edits: [
      {
        type: "clear_tool_uses_20250919",
        trigger: {type: "input_tokens", value: 30000},
        keep: {type: "tool_uses",value: 3},
        clear_at_least: {type: "input_tokens",value: 5000},
        exclude_tools: ["web_search"]
      }
    ]
```

**Thinking block:**
```
edits: [
      {
        type: "clear_thinking_20251015",
        keep: {type: "thinking_turns",value: 2} | 'all'
      }
   ]
```

and in the response field we get the data back in this form
```
"context_management": {
        "applied_edits": [
            {
                "type": "clear_thinking_20251015",
                "cleared_thinking_turns": 3,
                "cleared_input_tokens": 15000
            },
            {
                "type": "clear_tool_uses_20250919",
                "cleared_tool_uses": 8,
                "cleared_input_tokens": 50000
            }
        ]
    }
```

 - So I first wrote the type defintion for the both response and request body in the file `anthropic-message-api.ts ` 
 - Then added the `context_management` field in the provider options in the file `anthropic-message-options.ts`
 - Then added context_management to the request body in `getArgs()` method
 - Then parsed the response in `doGenerate()` method
 - Then parsed the streaming response in `doStream()` method
 - Then added `context_management` to the metadata interface

Right now , i was dealing with the test cases , many of the previously written test cases are failing , i think its because i have updated the metadata. I'll make the pr once all the test pass.

@0-Sandy 
Hey, it's great that you found a workaround, but I wanted to point out that the underlying issue still persists in the `huggingface` package.

**The Problem**: The Responses API format expects tool results using `type: 'function_call_output' ` , but the current Hugging Face provider implementation only handles `role: 'tool'` by throwing a warning and skipping the message.

**Why the workaround works**: The `openai` package correctly implements the `function_call_output `conversion , but the Hugging Face provider is missing this implementation.

I'd suggest reopening this issue so the Hugging Face provider can get the proper fix.

Thanks.

body:
If the developer adds a tool that the provider doesn’t actually support, the model itself will throw the error, which the developer can then handle.

The goal is to avoid blocking newly released provider tools just because the SDK hasn’t been updated yet. By passing through unknown tools instead of marking them as unsupported-tool, we can immediately use new provider-defined tools.

So the suggestion is:

Don’t block or warn about unknown tools in the SDK.

Pass them directly to the provider.

If the provider truly doesn’t support them, the provider will throw the error, not the SDK.


This way we can start using new built-in tools right away, without waiting for a new ai-sdk release.

body:
I'm also seeing this - it may have been triggered by some change in Sonnet inference. The problem seems to be related to prompting it to "use JSON" or "respond with JSON".

I have a PR review agent with a final answer tool.

In the Sonnet hidden system prompt, the model is instructed to format tool calls like this:
```xml
<antml:function_calls>
<antml:invoke name="TOOL_NAME">
<antml:parameter name="PARAMETER_NAME">PARAMETER_VALUE</antml:parameter>
<antml:parameter name="another_parameter">another value</antml:parameter>
</antml:invoke>
</antml:function_calls>
```
I'm pretty sure EXACTLY that text is sent to the LLM.



At the raw LLM level, a **correct** tool call would look like this:
```xml
<antml:function_calls>
  <antml:invoke name="final_answer">
    <antml:parameter name="event">COMMENT</antml:parameter>
    <antml:parameter name="comments">[{...}]</antml:parameter>
    <antml:parameter name="body">LGTM</antml:parameter>
  </antml:invoke>
</antml:function_calls>
```

But I think my instructions to "respond with JSON" confused the LLM and made it generate this instead:
```xml
<antml:function_calls>
  <antml:invoke name="final_answer">
    <antml:parameter name="$PARAMETER_NAME">{"event":"COMMENT","comments":[],"body":"LGTM"}</antml:parameter>
  </antml:invoke>
</antml:function_calls>
```

We've also seen it hallucinate `$JSON` and `$PARAMETER` as the name of the wrapper property, which makes sense because it doesn't know what it should use for the parameter name, if everything is going to be inside the single JSON blob.

Solutions: 
- stop asking it to "respond with JSON" and instead rely on the tool schemas. 
- as a more aggressive approach, provide an example of the XML format you want, in my case the second code block in this comment.

Some more information on the raw tool calling format here: https://arcfu.com/post/claude-json-solution/

body:
+1 — hitting this consistently without vision, just complex system prompts + cached multi-message format.

**Our scenario:**
- `generateObject` with `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (claude-sonnet-4-5)
- Large system prompt (~4K tokens with embedded taxonomies)
- Multi-message format with `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl` on system + context messages
- Complex nested Zod schema (12+ fields with multiple `z.enum()` arrays)
- No vision — pure text extraction

**Failure rate:** ~60% of calls return `{"$PARAMETER_NAME": {valid_data}}`, causing schema validation to fail. The data inside is always valid.

**Observation:** The wrapping is non-deterministic — identical inputs sometimes wrap, sometimes don't. Larger system prompts and more messages seem to increase the rate.

**Our workaround:** We fall back to `generateText` with `toolChoice: "required"` + a permissive Zod schema (strings instead of enums), then coerce the result. The `response.toolCalls[0].args` from `generateText` is always correctly unwrapped. This catches 100% of the failures.

```typescript
// Strict path — fails ~60% with $PARAMETER_NAME wrapping
const { object } = await generateObject({ model, schema: strictSchema, messages, ... });

// Fallback — always works, SDK correctly unwraps tool call args
const response = await generateText({
  model, messages, toolChoice: "required",
  tools: { extract: tool({ description: "...", parameters: permissiveSchema }) },
});
const result = coerce(response.toolCalls[0].args); // always unwrapped correctly
```

This confirms the issue extends beyond vision to any complex prompt + Anthropic tool calling scenario.

body:
Hi! I'd like to work on this. My understanding is that the current `experimental_RouterAgent` acts as a simple 1-depth router and lacks arbitrary deep chaining, state retention between steps, graph-based routing, or parallel execution branches. 

I'm planning to fix it by building an `AgentGraph` orchestration module in `ai/core` that introduces:
1. **GraphState Management**: A global, serializable state object that gets passed and merged sequentially through nodes.
2. **Nodes and Edges**: `AgentNode` wrappers for standard AI SDK agents, and conditional `Edge` routers (functions parsing node outputs to return the next target).
3. **Parallel Execution**: Async fan-out via `Promise.all` when routing to multiple edges, with a state-reducer pattern for merging before the next step.
4. **Graph Compiler**: A `.compile()` method to validate paths and return a unified generator/stream output.

Does this approach sound good? I can draft an architectural RFC PR of ~1000 lines demonstrating the state reducers and LangGraph-style multi-agent routing within the Vercel AI SDK patterns.

body:
Root Cause
The request.body returned by provider's doStream()/doGenerate() methods was being stored in step results and retained for the lifetime of the stream result. For requests with many images, this body contains base64-encoded image data (~33% larger than the original), causing significant memory retention.
With 500 images (~156MB), the base64-encoded body was ~208MB, and this was stored in step results without being garbage collected.

body:
@wladimiiir 
When using `stopWhen: stepCountIs()`, validation happens only once during the initial call. Subsequent steps bypass validation, which is why it doesn't throw errors even when tool results have heterogeneous arrays.

However, when manually iterating each call triggers validation again, causing the error.

**The Problem:**

```typescript
execute: ({limit = 20}) => ([
    {
        id: "1",
        state: "completed",
        startedAt: "2025-10-26T17:59:40.065Z",
        completedAt: "2025-10-26T18:00:31.713Z"
    },
    {
        id: "2",
        state: "archived",
        startedAt: undefined,
        completedAt: undefined
    }
])
```
infered type:

```typescript
Array<{
    id: string;
    state: string;
    startedAt: string | undefined;  // Key must exist
    completedAt: string | undefined; // Key must exist
}>
```
When this is JSON serialized , undefined values are stripped:

```typescript
[
    {"id": "1", "state": "completed", "startedAt": "2025-10-26T17:59:40.065Z", "completedAt": "2025-10-26T18:00:31.713Z"},
    {"id": "2", "state": "archived"}  // Keys missing
]
```

The schema expects the keys to exist even if undefined, but JSON serialization removed them entirely, causing validation to fail.

**Solution:**

For now , until it get fixed , what you can do is:

 - use null instead of undefined since null is preserved in JSON:

```typescript
{
    id: "2",
    state: "archived",
    startedAt: null,   
    completedAt: null
}
```

 - omit the keys entirely , this will make 'startedAt' and 'createdAt' optional in the inferred type:

 ```typescript
{
    id: "2",
    state: "archived",
}
```

+1 on a third state. The important distinction is `needs human consent` vs `cannot execute under policy`.

Prompting a user for something that policy will never allow creates a confusing UI and trains users to approve meaningless prompts. I would model it as a decision enum rather than overloading boolean:

- `allow`: execute
- `ask`: surface approval UI
- `block`: return a tool result with reason and do not execute

This also composes better with per-argument policies like path zones, spend limits, recipients, or production flags.

body:
Opened a PR to fix this: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/12914

The root cause is three interacting gaps in the tool approval pipeline:

1. `ignoreIncompleteToolCalls` doesn't filter `approval-requested` state
2. `convertToModelMessages` switch has no `approval-responded` case — falls through silently without producing a `tool-result`
3. `convertToLanguageModelPrompt` exempts approved tool-calls from the `MissingToolResultsError` validation but still sends them to the provider without matching results

The PR fixes all three:
- **Fix 1**: Adds `approval-requested` to the incomplete filter
- **Fix 2**: Adds `approval-responded` case — `approved: false` emits denied result, `approved: true` emits nothing (streamText handles execution)
- **Fix 3**: Tracks unresolved approved tool-call IDs and strips them from assistant messages before sending to the provider

body:
I would separate two things that are currently getting blurred here: an approval response is not a tool result, and a provider-bound transcript cannot contain a tool use without a terminal result for the same tool call.

For a needsApproval tool, approval should only move the call into one of two explicit next states:

1. Approved and executed: run the tool before the next provider request, then persist a tool result or tool error bound to the original toolCallId.
2. Approved but not yet executed: keep the conversation parked, or omit the pending tool call from provider context until execution produces a terminal result.

What should not happen is the middle state: approval is treated as resolved for validation, but conversion still emits the original tool use without a matching tool result.

I would pin the denied path the same way. A denial should produce a terminal denial result for the tool call, not a missing-result transcript and not a retryable pending approval.

Useful regression shape:

1. Start with an assistant message containing a needsApproval tool call.
2. Add an approval response from the client.
3. Simulate the resume or reconnect path before normal tool execution has produced output.
4. Assert the next provider request does not contain a bare tool use.
5. Assert the approved path executes exactly once and then emits one matching result.
6. Assert the denied path emits one terminal denial result and never calls the tool.

Boundary: architecture and regression-test feedback only; no claim about using this project or running its code.

body:
The issue is that `InferUIMessageToolCall` has a dynamic tool variant with `unknown` input:

```typescript
| (ToolCall<string, unknown> & { dynamic: true });
```

This causes TypeScript to fail narrowing `toolCall.input` when you check `toolCall.toolName`, since `unknown` pollutes the union.

Fix is straightforward - change `unknown` to `any`:

```diff
-  | (ToolCall<string, unknown> & { dynamic: true });
+  | (ToolCall<string, any> & { dynamic: true });
```

In `packages/ai/src/ui/ui-messages.ts`, line 495.

Dynamic tools don't have compile-time schemas anyway, so `any` is more accurate here. This lets the typed tools narrow correctly.

body:
Reproducible on `ai@6.0.168` via `resumeStream` when the server responds **204 No Content** (no active run to resume).

Stack:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'state')
    at Chat.makeRequest (chat.ts:761:41)
    at async AbstractChat.resumeStream (chat.ts:465:5)
```

Repro:
- `useChat({ id, resume: true, transport })` on a persistent conversation with no run currently in flight.
- Server GET `/chat/:id/stream` returns `204` (expected behaviour when there is nothing to resume).
- On mount, `resumeStream()` calls `makeRequest`, which throws before `this.activeResponse` is ever assigned.
- In `makeRequest`'s `finally`, the line `message: this.activeResponse!.state.message` (chat.ts:761) crashes.

Worth noting: the very next line `finishReason: this.activeResponse?.state.finishReason` already uses optional chaining. Applying `?.` to `message` as well (with a sensible fallback) would fix this whole class of issues without affecting the happy path.

Same crash shows up on `sendMessage()` when the POST fails fast (e.g. 409 conflict, content-length reject) before any chunk is delivered.

Local workaround: only pass `resume: true` after the server confirms an active run via the initial page payload, and silence this exact TypeError in `onError`. But the root fix belongs at chat.ts:761.

body: @lgrammel I'm currently struggling with the same issue and it's very difficult to find reliable information from OpenAI on this topic. However, I found one document that might be relevant to this topic: https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/responses_api/reasoning_items Specifically the part about [caching](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/responses_api/reasoning_items#caching): > In turn 2, any reasoning items from turn 1 are ignored and removed, since the model does not reuse reasoning items from previous turns. As a result, the fourth API call in the diagram cannot achieve a full cache hit, because those reasoning items are missing from the prompt. However, including them is harmless—the API will simply discard any reasoning items that aren’t relevant for the current turn. If reasoning items from previous turns are discarded anyway, maybe `pruneMessages` could remove the reasoning item and `itemId`s from `providerMetadata` for messages where a tool call was pruned. This would cause the tool call result to be inlcuded in the request to the Responses API instead of referenced via `item_reference`, but at least pruning would work.

@lgrammel here is what i found researching about this issue:

while going through official Claude docs I found this:
`
Tool choice limitation: Tool use with thinking only supports tool_choice: {"type": "auto"} (the default) or tool_choice: {"type": "none"}. Using tool_choice: {"type": "any"} or tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "..."} will result in an error because these options force tool use, which is incompatible with extended thinking.
`

the ai sdk achieves structured output by creating a fake tool and forcing the model to call it ,this conflicts with thinking mode which does not allow forced tool calling.

unlike the direct anthropic api which has native structured output , bedrock converse does not support this feature. bedrock only supports structured output through tool calling, which cannot be forced when thinking is enabled.

claude requires tool calling be optional while thinking is enabled -> ai sdk forces tool calling for structured output → conflict

tldr: I think , this is fundamentally a bedrock api limitation, they do not provide native structured output.

body:
I dug a bit deeper into the problem. 
The web_search provider-executed tool is not working with the Gateway provider because the Vercel AI Gateway backend server (which is separate from this SDK repo) doesn't seem to have logic to convert openai.web_search provider tools to the native OpenAI API format.

When you use openai.tools.webSearch(), the SDK converts it to a provider tool format like:

{
  "type": "provider",
  "id": "openai.web_search",
  "name": "web_search",
  "args": { "searchContextSize": "high" }
}

The Gateway backend should convert this to OpenAI's native format:

{ "type": "web_search", "search_context_size": "high" }

But instead, it returns an [unsupported-tool] warning.

The warning format is mismatched - The backend returns V2-style warnings ([type: 'unsupported-tool'](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)) but the SDK expects V3-style warnings ([type: 'unsupported'](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)).

The Fix
The fix needs to happen on the Vercel AI Gateway backend server (not in this SDK repository). The backend needs to:

Recognize OpenAI provider tools (openai.web_search, openai.file_search, openai.code_interpreter, etc.)
Convert them using the same logic as openai-responses-prepare-tools.ts:112-128

body:
Thanks for the clarification. Is there a specific reason for this limitation in the AI SDK, and is it something you plan to change in the future?

Float embeddings are usually the heaviest option. Other embedding types—such as `int8`, which we use—are significantly smaller, faster to work with, and require less storage and memory in the database. We’re considering migrating all vendor-specific modules to the AI SDK, but this limitation currently prevents us from doing so.

_The code that we run to get this output:_
```
const model = createTracedModel(createOpenAI({ apiKey: getOpenAIKey() })("gpt-5.2"), profileId, threadId);
const { output: decision } = await generateText({
  model,
  output: Output.object({ schema: decisionSchema }),
```

body:
Hi all, quick update
I found a workaround in case anyone is blocked on Gemini 3 Pro/Flash Preview + tools.

In @ai-sdk/google, the "auto" path currently returns:

```js
// node_modules/@ai-sdk/google/dist/index.mjs | Line 834 -> 839
case "auto":
  return {
    tools: [{ functionDeclarations }],
    toolConfig: { functionCallingConfig: { mode: "AUTO" } },
    toolWarnings
  };
```

If you let Gemini-3 default its own AUTO mode instead, tool calling behaves correctly again.

This conditional change fixes it for me:
```js
toolConfig: modelId.includes("gemini-3")
  ? void 0
  : { functionCallingConfig: { mode: "AUTO" } },
```

I’m attaching a small .patch that applies cleanly on @ai-sdk/google 3.0.1 (released a couple of hours ago) in case anyone wants to try it immediately. Hope this helps.

[@ai-sdk+google+3.0.1.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24317721/%40ai-sdk%2Bgoogle%2B3.0.1.patch)

> Looks like Logan from Google and team have identified the root issue and is rolling back: https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/gemini-responds-with-structured-json-like-output-only-when-function-calling-is-enabled/112993/48?u=mathewchan

I commented there:


Hey Logan and team, I don't think this is actually fully resolved. We're still seeing a variant of this problem in production with Gemini 3 Flash as of March 2026.

We run an AI automation platform that uses the Vercel AI SDK v6 with Gemini 3 Flash via the AI Gateway. We have a browser automation agent that uses multi-step tool calling (up to 99 steps for complex tasks like scraping ticket info from websites). The agent calls tools like navigate, click, screenshot, eval, etc.

What we're seeing is that Gemini 3 Flash dumps its entire internal reasoning process as visible text output between tool calls. After taking a screenshot, instead of just making the next tool call, the model writes things like:

"The screenshot shows a large Filters pane on the right that's blocking the view. I need to close the Filters pane or click View 47 Listings again. Wait, looking at the center: Showing 6 of 47 and a Show more button. Let's try to extract from the whole page again with a more robust script. Actually, let's just use get_text on the main container..."

This goes on for paragraphs. It also writes JavaScript code as visible text before putting the same code into an eval tool call. And sometimes it gets stuck in loops, repeating "wait, I'll click E41, actually I just run the URL" over and over.

We checked the AI SDK source and confirmed that sendReasoning defaults to true and reasoning parts are streamed as separate reasoning-start/delta/end events. The UI properly handles those with a collapsible component. But this reasoning text is NOT coming through as reasoning parts, it's coming through as regular text-delta events and gets stored as type: "text" in the database.

We also looked into setting thinkingConfig: { includeThoughts: true } but from what we can tell from the forums, that's purely observational and doesn't change the model's behavior. The model would still output reasoning as text regardless.

This is really painful because in a 55-step browser session, the user's chat gets flooded with the model's internal monologue. We are not setting functionCallingConfig explicitly since we go through the AI Gateway, so the patch from @AmrAbuElyazid shouldn't apply here.

Is there any update on the model separating its reasoning from its text output properly during multi-step function calling? This feels like the same fundamental issue, just a different symptom.

Thank you for the detail! Let me look more closely at this soon and follow up.

How would you like it to work, out of your proposed options, and do you already know or have a guess re: feasibility of them? For regenerating signatures, we'd have to resubmit the prompts in sequence, which I expect could be tricky depending on tools used. For incompatibility and retry it would be lossy, and depending on the model IIRC it might choke without any signatures.

Developers can effectively implement fix #2 by applying `only` to the Gateway provider options if there is an existing message. AI SDK also has [`pruneMessages`](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-ui/prune-messages#prunemessages), but of course using it is lossy.

This area is in general tricky and there is work planned ahead. I am interested in adding support in some manner to more easily bridge reasoning across providers and models in as non-lossy a manner as possible, more generally than for this single case in discussion. More design thinking to be done there, but it's helpful to get feedback on tradeoffs and approaches with this specific case to carry into that.

I appreciate you looking into this. I think getting a real error would be more helpful. Here is the better response I have combining what I and Claude observed.

## My Preference: Option #2 (Don't fail over if messages exist)

**Why:** It's the simplest and least lossy approach. Here's my reasoning:

### The Current Behavior is Confusing

Right now when this happens, I get an error about "missing thought_signature" which is **not the real problem**. The real problem is whatever caused Vertex to fail (tool error, 503, etc.). By failing over, the gateway hides the actual error and shows a misleading one.

### What I'd Prefer

If there's an existing conversation with thought_signatures:
- **Don't fail over** - just let the Vertex error bubble up
- This way I see the real error: "Invalid JSON response" or "503" or whatever
- I can actually debug and fix my tool code instead of chasing thought_signature issues

If it's a fresh conversation (no existing messages):
- **Fail over freely** - there's no thought_signature incompatibility yet
- This preserves the Gateway's value for handling provider outages

### Feasibility Thoughts

You mentioned developers can implement this by checking for existing messages before applying Gateway provider options. That seems totally doable and not lossy at all.

Something like:
```typescript
// Pseudo-code for gateway routing logic
if (messages.length > 0 && hasThoughtSignatures(messages)) {
  // Stick with primary provider, don't fail over
  // Let the real error surface
} else {
  // Fresh conversation, fail over freely
}
```

### Why Not Option #1 (Regenerate)?

I agree with your concern - replaying tool executions could have side effects (like actually sending that email twice, or creating duplicate database records). Too risky.

### Why Not Option #3 (Retry without signature)?

If the model requires thought_signatures for quality, stripping them seems worse than just surfacing the real error.

### The Bigger Picture

The current failover behavior optimizes for **availability** (keep the conversation going at all costs), but at the expense of **debuggability** (what's actually broken?).

For my use case, I'd rather have a clear error I can fix than a working-but-degraded model that's hiding the root cause.

---

**Bottom line:** Option #2 feels like the right tradeoff. Fail over on fresh conversations, stick with primary provider on existing ones. This avoids cross-provider incompatibility entirely while keeping the original error visible for debugging.

Does that align with where you're thinking of taking this?

body:
Strong +1 on this. Skills as first-class tool constructors would unlock a whole category of capabilities that don't fit the "LLM figures it out" pattern — specifically mathematical computation.

LLMs are great at deciding WHAT to optimize but terrible at actually running the optimization. A skill that wraps deterministic algorithms fixes this cleanly. Example use case: an agent managing A/B tests needs Thompson Sampling to pick the winner, or a scheduling agent needs an LP solver for constraint satisfaction.

For an MCP-compatible approach that works today with any provider:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oraclaw": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@oraclaw/mcp-server"]
    }
  }
}
```

This exposes 12 mathematical tools to the agent:
- **Bandit optimization** — A/B testing, model selection (UCB1/Thompson/LinUCB)
- **LP/MIP solver** — scheduling, allocation, constraint satisfaction
- **Monte Carlo simulation** — risk analysis, confidence intervals
- **Anomaly detection** — cost spikes, latency monitoring (Z-score/IQR)
- **Graph analytics** — PageRank, community detection, bottleneck identification
- **Risk analysis** — portfolio VaR/CVaR

Also available as npm packages (`@oraclaw/bandit`, `@oraclaw/solver`, `@oraclaw/simulate`, etc.) if direct tool constructors are preferred over MCP.

[OraClaw](https://github.com/Whatsonyourmind/oraclaw) — 17 algorithms, all <25ms. Free tier for testing, $9/mo for production.

Would a native skill constructor support wrapping MCP servers, or would it be a separate interface? That distinction matters a lot for tool providers.

After further investigation, I found that the issue I encountered may be more closely related to #11348, because when using Vercel AI Gateway, whether it’s the GPT series or the Gemini series models, I ran into the same error. It should be because AI Gateway returns `finishReason: undefined`, causing the AI SDK not to parse the `output`.

------------------------------
We encountered a similar issue after migrating from AI SDK v5 to v6.

**Environment:**
- `ai`: 6.0.3
- Model: `gemini-3-flash` (via Vercel AI Gateway)
- No tools being used

**Issue:**
After migrating from `generateObject` to `generateText` + `Output.object()` following the v6 migration guide, we started seeing `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError` failures.

**A/B Test:**
We ran both APIs in parallel with identical inputs:

```typescript
// This succeeds
const { object } = await generateObject({
  model: google('gemini-3-flash'),
  schema: mySchema,
  system: SYSTEM_PROMPT,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: userPrompt }],
  temperature: 0,
});

// This fails with AI_NoObjectGeneratedError
const { output } = await generateText({
  model: google('gemini-3-flash'),
  output: Output.object({ schema: mySchema }),
  system: SYSTEM_PROMPT,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: userPrompt }],
  temperature: 0,
});
```

**Result:**
- `generateObject`: Returns valid structured output
- `generateText` + `Output.object`: Throws `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError`

This suggests the issue may not be limited to code execution scenarios, but affects `Output.object()` with Gemini 3 models more broadly.

body:
> an ideal solution would be the one where we only make changes at the provider level

@aayush-kapoor I don't think it is.

This approach is limiting since:
- non-tech-savvy users suffer greatly from having to process generated images before they can even display them;
- it introduces an artificial bottleneck for the sake of backwards compatibility: I can generate thousands of images and, if the model returns URLs, just provide S3 links and stream them without making the server do extra work; if a provider already returns hosted URLs, the SDK should be able to surface them directly instead of forcing an extra download/re-encode step.

Adding e.g. `readonly imageUrl?: string` to `GeneratedFile` (alongside existing `uint8Array` and `base64`) would greatly benefit users and better reflect the current state of image gen APIs/models (e.g. [Grok Imagine](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/images/generation#quick-start), [fal.ai](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/overview), [Replicate](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/output-files#working-with-urls), [OpenAI Images API / DALL·E with `response_format: "url"`](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/images/create)).

If this makes sense, I'm happy to create a PR implementing it.

body:
it's not that explicit caching doesn't work with tool calls, it's that if you're using a cached object then you can't modify the SI and tools after (since they have already been cached) i.e. explicit caching DOES work with tools

implicit caching works inherently with google models - so most likely the conditions required for your request to hit context cache aren't being met.

i just tested an example to see if there's a problem with the AI SDK where tools + caching doesn't work but i received cache tokens usage data, which means it's up to the model provider to decide when to use cache. hope this is helpful; will be closing this issue since this is expected behaviour but feel free to ask questions on this thread

body:
Additional Info for this issue:

The first error occurs because `chunking_strategy` is required for inputs longer than 30 seconds. For an input shorter than 30 seconds, the AI SDK will return a valid response, but it will be in `response_format` `json` which defeats a lot of the motivation for using this model.

The second error occurs because setting a `providerOptions` passes defaults for properties that are not explicitly passed. 

As pointed out by OP 
https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/8246#discussion_r2297318020

passing providerOptions defaults the model to `response_format` `verbose_json` which is not supported by the model. If it was supported, then we would be back to the first error because of the lack of `chunking_strategy`

So this issue is two fold
1) A valid `chunking_strategy` ought to reach the API
2) Supporting this model in a meaningful way means supporting `diarize_json` formats. Likely this means defaulting the providerOptions to this type for this model and enhancing the zod validation to work with the `TranscriptionDiarized` response from OpenAI

body:
## Bug Reproduction

**Bug was reproduced.**

Branch: [`main`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/main)
PR: [successful reproduction pull request](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/17006)

### Details

- Added `examples/ai-functions/src/reproduction/express-compression-ui-message-stream.ts` as a runnable `Express/compression` reproduction, with supporting dev dependencies in `examples/ai-functions/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- The reproduction expects Express + compression to deliver the first AI SDK UI message stream chunk within 500ms, matching the user-visible streaming behavior expected from the Express UI message stream helper.
- The uncompressed control route streamed promptly: first chunk arrived at 12ms across 6 reads.
- The compressed route reproduced the reported failure: `content-encoding` was `gzip`, the first readable chunk arrived only after 1024ms, and the entire response arrived in a single read after the delayed stream had effectively completed.
- No live provider was needed because the issue is `Express/compression` transport behavior around `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse`, not provider output.

### Relevant Documentation

- https://ai-sdk.dev/cookbook/api-servers/express
- https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-ui/pipe-ui-message-stream-to-response
- https://expressjs.com/en/resources/middleware/compression/

Thanks for the detailed write-up! Before moving forward with the proposed fix, could you provide a concrete test case that demonstrates `isParsableJson()` returning `true` for incomplete JSON?

For example, a specific string value where:
```typescript
const partialJson = '{"code": "line1\\nline2\\n...'; // incomplete
isParsableJson(partialJson) // returns true (incorrectly)
```

The error message in your logs (`Unterminated string in JSON at position 3337`) suggests the emitted input was *invalid* JSON — which would mean `isParsableJson()` returned `false`, not a false positive.

A reproducible test input would help confirm the root cause before we change the emission logic. It's possible the bug is elsewhere (different code path, race condition, provider-specific chunking behavior, etc.).
author: lgrammel
Aparnap2

body:
I took a look at this and I think the root cause might be different from what's described.

From what I can tell, `isParsableJson` shouldn't be able to trigger prematurely with well-formed deltas. A prefix of a valid JSON object can't itself be valid JSON, since you'd need a closing `}` that doesn't exist mid-stream. I wrote a quick check confirming this for various patterns (nested objects, arrays, booleans, etc.) and none had a valid-JSON prefix.

The error message (`Unterminated string in JSON at position 3337`) also seems to point away from a false positive. It suggests the emitted input was *invalid* JSON, meaning `isParsableJson` returned `false`, not `true`.

One possibility I'm thinking is **snapshot-style argument streaming**. If the provider sends the full accumulated arguments each chunk instead of just the new delta, the `+=` at [line 609](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts#L609) would produce garbled strings like:

```
'{"code":"he' + '{"code":"hello"' → '{"code":"he{"code":"hello"'
```

This would be consistent with the `Unterminated string` error, since the garbled string would get emitted from `flush()` ([lines 652](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/openai-compatible/src/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts#L652)) and fail downstream parsing. I wasn't able to find documentation confirming whether ByteDance ARK sends snapshots vs deltas though, so this is just a theory.

Would it be possible to capture the raw SSE chunks from the provider? Something like logging `toolCallDelta.function.arguments` on each chunk inside the `transform()` handler would help pin down the exact cause.

body:
MCP Apps integration would be a great addition to the AI SDK. One pattern that works well with the existing MCP tool support: specialized computation servers that handle tasks LLMs waste tokens on.

For mathematical/optimization capabilities that agents frequently need but can't do natively, there's an MCP server ready to integrate:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oraclaw": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@oraclaw/mcp-server"]
    }
  }
}
```

This gives AI SDK agents 12 mathematical tools:
- **Bandit optimization** — A/B testing, model selection (UCB1/Thompson/LinUCB)
- **LP/MIP solver** — scheduling, allocation, constraint satisfaction
- **Monte Carlo simulation** — risk analysis, confidence intervals
- **Anomaly detection** — cost spikes, latency monitoring
- **Graph analytics** — PageRank, community detection
- **Risk analysis** — VaR/CVaR

Works with `generateText` and `streamText` today via MCP tools. The agent reasons about the problem, the algorithm handles the computation deterministically.

Also available as npm packages (`@oraclaw/bandit`, `@oraclaw/solver`, `@oraclaw/simulate`, etc.) for direct tool construction.

[OraClaw](https://github.com/Whatsonyourmind/oraclaw) — 17 algorithms, all <25ms. Free tier for testing, $9/mo for production.

When MCP Apps lands, would it support auto-discovery of MCP servers from a registry, or would each app need manual configuration?

body: @joetifa2003 @ghostyfreak I'm not with Vercel, but I've followed the changes in this PR. `DurableAgent` was the first iteration, located in `@workflow/ai` or so (i.e. in the Workflow SDK, not in the AI SDK). It reimplemented most of what `ToolLoopAgent` does because there were no resuable primitives available, it was a small monolith. Actually, the reimplementation just had stubs or very simplified code in many places, so lots of things didn't work as expected. Then that code was copied to a branch in this repo (the AI SDK). Step by step, the `ToolLoopAgent` was split up and the individual steps were made reusable that the `ToolLoopAgent` stitches together. Somewhere in the process, `DurableAgent` was renamed to `WorkflowAgent`, and it uses the same building blocks. The PR is very valuable because it removes duplication, replaces stubs with fully functioning code and ensures that both approaches stay in sync further on.

body:
Adding some additional findings in case it's useful for the fix.

The patch in the linked gist fixes the continuation in `streamText` (adds `hasProviderExecutedToolResultsNeedingContinuation` to the do-while condition) but the same fix is missing from the `generateText` path. `ToolLoopAgent.generate()` calls `generateText` internally, so the loop exits after step 1 even with the patch applied.

The `generateText` do-while at `src/generate-text/generate-text.ts` still has only the original two conditions:

```
(clientToolCalls.length > 0 && clientToolOutputs.length === clientToolCalls.length || pendingDeferredToolCalls.size > 0)
```

There's also a second issue: even if continuation is added to `generateText`, the `toResponseMessages` change in the patch filters gateway tool results out of the next step's message history (`_isGatewayTool` check). So step 2 would run without the search results in context. This was added to prevent streaming duplication but it affects the non-streaming path too.

Our current workaround: drop `Output.object` from the research agent entirely and have it produce prose output, which gets injected as `<external_evidence>` into the evaluator prompt. Works fine since the evaluator reads text anyway. Sharing in case it helps narrow the scope of the upstream fix.

Same symptom: generateText/streaming loop ends with finishReason: "stop" (sometimes "other") while a tool-call part is still pending — full input present, no result, no error thrown. Concrete example on openai/gpt-5.4-mini (routed via Azure through the AI Gateway), ai@7.0.0:

```
{
  "type": "tool-sql_read",
  "input": {
    "query": "SELECT DISTINCT sender_type::text AS sender_type FROM messages WHERE id = '...' ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 20",
    "reason": "Need valid sender_type values to identify the latest agent message."
  },
  "state": "input-available",
  "toolCallId": "call_X5gEY1xcQtlz9NZCcK01Rb3v"
}
```

This is a ToolLoopAgent with a normal execute function on every tool (so it's not the "no execute defined" case mentioned above) - the loop just never gets a chance to run it because the stream already ended. Across our production traffic in the last few days we've seen this ~30 times, dominated by gpt-5.4-mini, so it doesn't look xAI-specific.

body:
> ### Description
> When using `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse` with Next.js 13.0.5 Pages Router API routes, the response is buffered entirely before being sent to the client, resulting in "fake streaming" where all SSE events arrive at the same timestamp.
> 
> ## Reproduction steps
> 1. Create a Next.js Pages Router API route using `streamText` and `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse`:
> 
> `// pages/api/chat.ts import { streamText } from "ai"; import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
> 
> export default async function handler(req, res) { const result = streamText({ model: openai("gpt-4o"), messages: req.body.messages, });
> 
> result.pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse(res); }`
> 
> 1. Observe in browser DevTools Network → EventStream tab that all messages have identical timestamps
> 
> ## Expected behavior
> SSE events should arrive incrementally with different timestamps as they are generated by the model.
> 
> ## Actual behavior
> All events are buffered and sent at once after the entire response is complete.
> 
> ## Workaround
> Manually pipe the stream with explicit headers to disable buffering:
> 
> `res.socket?.setNoDelay(true); res.setHeader("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8"); res.setHeader("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-transform"); res.setHeader("Content-Encoding", "none"); res.flushHeaders();
> 
> const stream = result.toUIMessageStream(); const sseStream = stream.pipeThrough(new TransformStream({ transform(chunk, controller) { controller.enqueue(`data: ${JSON.stringify(chunk)}\n\n`); }, }));
> 
> const reader = sseStream.getReader(); while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; res.write(value); } res.end();`
> 
> ## Root cause
> The internal `writeToServerResponse` function in the SDK doesn't:
> 
> 1. Set `Content-Encoding: none` to disable compression
> 2. Call `res.flushHeaders()` before writing
> 3. Disable Nagle's algorithm with `socket.setNoDelay(true)`
> 
> ## AI SDK Version
> `ai: ^6.0.68`
> 
> ## Environment
> * Next.js 13.0.5 (Pages Router)
> * Node.js 18+
> 
> ### AI SDK Version
> _No response_
> 
> ### Code of Conduct
> * [x]  I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

## Bug Reproduction

**Bug was reproduced.**

Branch: [`main`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/main)
PR: [successful reproduction pull request](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/17007)

### Details

- Added `examples/ai-functions/src/reproduction/issue-12233-next-pages-buffering.ts`, a runnable reproduction that creates a Next.js 13.0.5 Pages Router app and probes `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse` with browser-like `Accept-Encoding`.
- Expected the SDK SSE events to arrive incrementally with spaced timestamps as the stream enqueues chunks every 200 ms.
- Observed the SDK route returned `content-encoding: gzip` and all six decoded SSE events arrived in one decoded chunk with `eventSpanMs: 0`.
- The manual workaround route in the same app returned `content-encoding: none` and delivered events incrementally over about 814 ms, confirming the Pages route can stream when compression buffering is disabled.

### Relevant Documentation

- https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-ui/pipe-ui-message-stream-to-response
- https://ai-sdk.dev/cookbook/api-servers/node-http-server
- https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes

body:
## Bugfix

Created bugfix and updated PR: #17007

### Summary

Set `Content-Encoding: none` and `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` for UI message ServerResponse streams, and make ServerResponse stream writes disable Nagle and flush headers before writing chunks.

### Testing

Added regression coverage for `writeToServerResponse` flushing headers and disabling Nagle before chunk writes, and updated `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse`/`streamText` header expectations.

body:
just talked about this with @gr2m and we aligned on the following naming conventions for the types going forward:

```
{ProviderName}{ModelType}{OptionalModelTypeSuffix}Options
```

* `ProviderName`: e.g. Anthropic, Google, OpenAI
* `ModelType`: e.g. `LanguageModel`, `ImageModel`
* `OptionalModelSuffix`: only relevant if there are multiple variants of a model type, e.g. for OpenAI or OpenAI compatible providers `Chat` and `Responses`

Examples:
* `AnthropicLanguageModelOptions`
* `GoogleImageModelOptions`
* `OpenAILanguageModelChatOptions`

It makes sense to drop the "provider" term entirely from the name because the options are specific to the model type (and their underlying API endpoint spec); it also would fit nicely, should we eventually rename `providerOptions` to `options` (which is _not_ part of this issue).

body:
This is a nasty class of failure because costs can keep accumulating while the loop makes no progress.

One pragmatic mitigation (in addition to SDK loop controls) is adding an external pre-flight “fuse”: before each expensive step (model call / tool call), do a quick check that tracks a hash of the action/tool + args within a short sliding window, and hard-stop once it’s clearly repeating.

I’m building ProceedGate with this approach (≤5 repeats allow, 6–10 gray, 11+ block; plus optional budget caps). It’s not meant to replace AI SDK loop control—just to fail-safe when loops slip through.

Docs/quickstart: https://proceedgate.dev/docs.html. If it’s helpful, I can share a minimal wrapper pattern for streamText + tools.
author: loquit-tud

body:
Infinite loops in multi-step tool calling is one of the most common production failures in agentic systems. From building loop detection and prevention:

**The root cause pattern**: When `prepareStep` forces a specific tool via `toolChoice`, the model complies — but if it also wants to call other tools (which it just did in the previous step), the forced tool call doesn't satisfy the model's intent, so it re-enters the loop trying to call both the forced tool and its preferred tools. The forced `toolChoice` prevents the model from expressing "I'm done with tools" which is the natural loop termination signal.

**Three-layer loop detection**:

1. **Syntactic** — Exact action sequence matching. Check if the last N steps repeat the same tool call sequence. If the same (tool_name, tool_args_hash) appears 3+ times consecutively, it's a loop. Fast and cheap to detect.

2. **Semantic** — Output similarity. Embed the last K step outputs and check cosine similarity. Two different tool calls producing semantically identical results (>0.95 similarity) indicates a semantic loop — different actions, same dead end.

3. **Progress-based** — Is the task getting closer to completion? Define a measurable "distance to goal" and check if it's decreasing. If 5+ steps pass without progress, the agent is stuck regardless of whether it looks like a traditional loop.

**Breaking the loop**: Detection without recovery is just a fancy way to crash. When a loop is detected:
1. First detection: inject a "step back, your last N actions were identical" message and remove the forced `toolChoice` for one step
2. Second detection: force a different tool or model to break the behavioral pattern
3. Third detection: escalate — return what you have with a `loop_detected` flag

**Budget-aware loop protection**: Each iteration of the loop costs tokens. Set a per-task cost ceiling and check it on every step. Loops burn budget fast — a /bin/bash.50 ceiling stops a runaway loop after ~10-20 iterations rather than letting it run indefinitely.

Related architecture on loop detection and agent coordination: https://blog.kinthai.ai/221-agents-multi-agent-coordination-lessons

body:
@gr2m Reviewing this, in terms of different provider implementations, I have 2 additions I don't think this was covering yet:

- Fireworks also uses async image generation with polling for some models for which it is required, see #11159.
- Replicate has an interesting pattern where they _may_ fall back to a polling approach if the image or video generation takes too long - it doesn't _always_ require polling. https://replicate.com/docs/reference/http#predictions.create-description
    - Generating an image taking more than 60 seconds is unlikely, but technically we lack support for this at the moment. We _do_ support it for video generation, where it's of course more likely to be relevant.

A few thoughts on the future first-class API abstraction:

1. How do you think about this across different providers? Would e.g. the `poll` option object only be allowed for providers that offer that (polling endpoint, request/task IDs, etc.)? Or would we always allow it and for providers that return the result immediately simply skip polling?
2. How do we support the Replicate behavior? E.g. if a video generation task takes only 30 seconds, I suppose we don't need to poll for that?
    - It would be interesting to see if there's a way to enforce polling. As in "even if this task might take 10 seconds, we want to get a task ID back and poll right away". That might help implement our API more consistently.
3. I think it's important to consider that this goes beyond video generation. While in practice it's unlikely to be needed for 90+% of image generation efforts, some providers (like Replicate) already have this in place for image generation. And if we think about e.g. a future model which allows you to generate 20 images in one job, that would likely require polling too.
4. What about exposing the polling mechanism through the top-level API? Maybe there's a use-case where the caller doesn't want to wait for polling until it's done - maybe they just want to get the request/task ID and occasionally re-check. Or maybe it's a task that is expected to take 5 hours, and the caller wants to store that request/task ID and check if it's done at some future point.
    - It feels a bit low-level to expose this, but I think it's worth thinking about. It would give developers more control and avoids making lots of requests if the developer is expecting for this to take a while, but doesn't want to keep `await`ing for the result. I think it becomes a more relevant concern the longer a task is expected to take.
    - Using a webhook would be a good alternative to this, but as far as I understand we may not be able to support that for every provider, since it depends on the provider?

Dancer,

### TLDR
The current AI SDK adapter for Transcription supports one iterable through the segments property. Many transcription apis support returning multiple iterables. Exposing body allows for fixes such as #12408 and #12120 to land with more sensible type safe examples.

Those PRs resolve some inconsistencies in the AI sdks transcription support for both openai and groq

#12408

need add system prompt  to make phase "commentary" work
```
# Working with the user

You interact with the user through a terminal. You have 2 ways of communicating with the users:  
- Share intermediary updates in \`commentary\` channel.  
- After you have completed all your work, send a message to the \`final\` channel.  

## Intermediary updates

- Intermediary updates go to the \`commentary\` channel.
- User updates are short updates while you are working, they are NOT final answers.
- You use 1-2 sentence user updates to communicate progress and new information to the user as you are doing work.
- Do not begin responses with conversational interjections or meta commentary. Avoid openers such as acknowledgements (“Done —”, “Got it”, “Great question, ”) or framing phrases.
- You provide user updates frequently, every 20s.
- Before exploring or doing substantial work, you start with a user update acknowledging the request and explaining your first step. You should include your understanding of the user request and explain what you will do. Avoid commenting on the request or using starters such as "Got it -" or "Understood -" etc.
- When exploring, e.g. searching, reading files, you provide user updates as you go, every 20s, explaining what context you are gathering and what you've learned. Vary your sentence structure when providing these updates to avoid sounding repetitive - in particular, don't start each sentence the same way.
- After you have sufficient context, and the work is substantial, you provide a longer plan (this is the only user update that may be longer than 2 sentences and can contain formatting).
- Before performing file edits of any kind, you provide updates explaining what edits you are making.
- As you are thinking, you very frequently provide updates even if not taking any actions, informing the user of your progress. You interrupt your thinking and send multiple updates in a row if thinking for more than 100 words.
- Tone of your updates MUST match your personality.
```

body:
Did some research:

### Overall naming - thinking vs reasoning?

* thinking: 7 (including Anthropic and Google)
* reasoning: 4 (including OpenAI)
* some have a mix of both terms

**Winner:** "thinking"

### Enabling it - explicit via flag vs implicit just by setting effort / level / budget?

* explicit: 7 (including Anthropic)
* implicit: 4 (including Google and OpenAI)

**Winner:** explicit flag (called `type` in almost all cases, with value "enabled")

### Effort - require token budget vs enum string to describe effort/level?

* both: 3 (including Anthropic and Google, though they both consider the "budget" approach deprecated)
* effort/level: 3 (including OpenAI)
* budget: 4

**Winner:** _probably_ effort/level (most providers use "effort" as term, pretty much only Google uses "level")

### Effort possible values

* All 6 support "low" and "high"
* 5 also support "medium".

**Winner:** definitely "low" and "high", maybe also "medium"?

cc @lgrammel @gr2m

body:
Capturing some updates here on the proposed direction, based on the feedback and other async discussions (cc @lgrammel):

- Use **`reasoning`** (not `thinking`) as the top-level v7 abstraction, to align with existing AI SDK naming.
- Model it as a **single flat enum** (no nesting), e.g. `reasoning?: "provider-default" | "none" | "low" | "medium" | "high"` where **`"none"` effectively means "disabled".
- **Do not set an AI SDK default effort level, instead use `"provider-default"`**; this should mean “use provider/model default behavior” (avoid repeating the “temperature: 0” default mistake).
- For models/providers that **require a token budget** instead of effort, allow the provider’s language model to **optionally map effort → budget**; otherwise **warn and ignore**. Callers will need to continue using `providerOptions` for those cases.
- If a provider supports only some enum values (e.g. no `medium`), the provider should **coerce to the closest lower supported value and warn**, rather than ignoring the setting. Only if the given value is the lowest possible excluding "none" (i.e. "low"), if that value is not supported it should be mapped to the next higher one.

Whether the response should include reasoning tokens or not is a related, but somewhat separate consideration. If we include this in the top-level API, I think it should simply be another top-level field (again, to avoid nesting).

Follow up questions, based on the feedback:
1. Should we include an "extra high" and "extra low" value in our top-level enum? If so, should we call them "xhigh" and "minimal" (in alignment with OpenAI and OpenRouter) or something else?
2.  Should we add a top-level boolean for whether to include reasoning tokens? e.g. `includeReasoningTokens: bool`?

Curious on your perspectives.
author: felixarntz

body:
I like the general direction.

Personally, I feel quite strong though about an object with at least `effort` and `max_tokens` parameters though. 

Rational:
1. While `effort` is becoming more and more common, it's more of a closed-source concept (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic). Most open-source models only support a more basic `max_tokens` parameter. 
2. While Anthropic is phasing out `max_tokens`, it actually allows side-by-side usage together with `effort` for fine-tuning of behavior (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort)

In terms of the actual values, would suggest to align with OpenAI / Openrouter: `none` | `minimal` | `low` | `medium` | `high` | `xhigh` (no need to reinvent the wheel).
author: heiwen

body:
@heiwen 
> While `effort` is becoming more and more common, it's more of a closed-source concept (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic). Most open-source models only support a more basic `max_tokens` parameter.

While some providers or models still use the numeric approach, it's not quite feasible as an abstraction layer. Different models have different overall tokens limits, and once we abstract something, there is a uniform behavior expectation. But that doesn't work with a numeric reasoning budget: While passing e.g. 50k might be fine for a model with 200k overall max tokens, it wouldn't be reasonable with a model with 4k overall max tokens.

Exposing only an enum value in the top-level API means this is not a concern for the caller, and can be solved at the provider implementation level. Providers can control individually how they would map the enum values to numeric budgets, if needed.

> In terms of the actual values, would suggest to align with OpenAI / Openrouter: `none` | `minimal` | `low` | `medium` | `high` | `xhigh` (no need to reinvent the wheel).

This makes sense to me. Aligning with this superset also means we support a more granular baseline - always simpler to broaden, if a provider only supports less granularity, than to make it more granular.
author: felixarntz

body: 100% agree with the ideal of `effort` being the sole driver. In practice though, especially for OSS models, implementing that is a real constraint and hiding `maxTokens` as a top-level control can bias against them. Just my 2¢, I’ll stop nitpicking now 😄

I checked this against current `main` and this appears to be resolved/stale now.

Evidence from `vercel/ai@19736eedbbd8ad3c6d8c95873f1d16da85393d60`:

- `packages/openai-compatible/src/openai-compatible-provider.ts` extends `ProviderV4`.
- The chat, completion, embedding, and image model implementations all declare `readonly specificationVersion = 'v4'`.
- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` is currently `3.0.0-canary.54` in this checkout.

Validation run locally:

```text
corepack pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/openai-compatible type-check
EXIT_CODE=0

corepack pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/openai-compatible test:node
Test Files  8 passed (8)
Tests       233 passed (233)
EXIT_CODE=0
```

I also checked for related PRs using `gh search prs` for `12615` and `openai-compatible specificationVersion ProviderV4` and did not find an open or closed PR tied to this issue.

If the warning still reproduces on a published package, it may be a release/channel mismatch rather than a source issue on `main`.

This is related to the same underlying issue as #10980. When a user sends a new message while a tool is in `approval-requested` state, `convertToModelMessages` produces a `tool-call` without a matching `tool-result`, causing the provider error.

PR https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/12914 fixes this by adding `approval-requested` to the `ignoreIncompleteToolCalls` filter — a tool awaiting user decision is incomplete and should be stripped when building model messages for the next request.

body:
I'd like to work on this.

Looking at `packages/google/src/google-prepare-tools.ts`, the `toolConfig.functionCallingConfig.mode` type is currently `'AUTO' | 'NONE' | 'ANY'` — missing `'VALIDATED'`.

One design question: Gemini's `VALIDATED` mode is a global `functionCallingConfig` setting, while `strict` in the AI SDK is per-tool. If some tools have `strict: true` and others don't, we need a policy:

1. **If any tool has `strict: true`, use `VALIDATED` mode** — safest, matches the intent of requesting strict validation
2. **Only use `VALIDATED` when all tools have `strict: true`** — more conservative

I'd lean toward option 1, since a user setting `strict: true` on any tool clearly wants schema validation enforced.

The implementation would:
- Add `'VALIDATED'` to the mode union type
- Check if any tool in the `tools` array has `strict: true`
- If so, set mode to `'VALIDATED'` instead of the default for that toolChoice type
- This applies to `auto`, `required`, and `tool` choice types

Would appreciate guidance on the preferred approach before submitting a PR.

I found that the suggested workaround unfortunately does not work as expected. `withUserAgentSuffix` always appends the SDK-generated parts to an existing `user-agent` header rather than replacing it, so the invalid tokens remain in the final value regardless.

The only reliable workaround without the upstream fix would be a local proxy that rewrites the header before forwarding.

I also found that `ai-sdk/openai-compatible/${VERSION}` (in `openai-compatible-provider.ts`) introduces a third invalid token via the same code path. The fix in #12800 covers this as well, since `normalizeUserAgentPart()` is applied to all suffix parts passed to `withUserAgentSuffix`.

body:
Great proposal! A few thoughts from production experience with multi-provider skill management:

## On the file content format (Open question)

**Strong preference for Option C** (string = UTF-8, Uint8Array = binary). Here's why:

1. **DX matters for adoption** — Skills are predominantly Markdown + Python/JS. Requiring base64 for a `.md` file feels like unnecessary friction:
   ```typescript
   // Option A/D: awkward
   const content = Buffer.from(markdownSource).toString('base64');
   
   // Option C: natural
   const content = markdownSource;
   ```

2. **Precedent exists** — Node.js `fs.writeFile` accepts string or Buffer. Same pattern here.

3. **Auto-detect (B) is fragile** — Legitimate skill content could look like base64. Silent misinterpretation would be a debugging nightmare.

## Additional considerations

### 1. Skill validation before upload

Both providers validate `SKILL.md` structure server-side, but errors are opaque. Consider a local `experimental_validateSkill()` that catches common issues (missing required fields, invalid tool schemas) before the round-trip.

### 2. Skill testing/dry-run mode

In production, we often want to test a skill update before promoting it. Anthropic's single-pointer model makes this tricky. Would the SDK support a pattern like creating a draft skill, testing it, then promoting?

### 3. Error types

The `deleteFromApi()` addition is a good call. Consider also defining typed errors for skill-specific failures: `SkillValidationError`, `SkillQuotaError`, `SkillNotFoundError`.

---

Happy to help test the implementation. We're building on the AI SDK at [RevolutionAI](https://revolutionai.io) and would be early adopters.

body:
@xXMrNidaXx I'm still on the fence about base64 vs plain-text for the `string` part of `string | Uint8Array`:

* **Why plaintext would be better:**
    * Skills are predominantly plain text, so expecting base64 would be confusing.
    * Node APIs like `fs.writeFile` treat `string` as plain text, so it's a common convention already there.
* **Why base64 would be better:**
    * The existing AI SDK APIs consistently treat the `string` part of `string | Uint8Array` as base64. Granted, this was all built exclusively with media files in mind. But it might still be confusing in terms of consistency.
    * Skills are not _exclusively_ plain text. In fact providers like Anthropic and OpenAI support packaging up the entire skill as a ZIP.

At the end of the day, both approaches have consistency concerns to some extent. Since binary files can still be provided via `Uint8Array`, I'm inclined to agree with you that we should treat `string` as plain text. Just not 100% sure yet.

body:
The production example here also clarifies the remaining gap in #5018/#7246.

The issue is no longer whether the SDK can parse `Retry-After`; short values are already supported. The unresolved case is when the provider’s authoritative recovery time exceeds the SDK’s local short-wait policy.

A long `Retry-After` should not automatically become ordinary exponential retry, but it is not necessarily globally terminal either. It should be evaluated against an explicit total execution budget and then produce one of a few clear outcomes: wait, defer/resume, route away temporarily, or terminate the current execution while preserving the recovery time for the caller.

Would the maintainers prefer this to be expressed through `retryTimeout`, an `onRetry` callback, or a typed error that exposes the parsed recovery timestamp?

body:
+1, swallowing AbortError is dangerous in multi-step tool loops because callers can’t distinguish “clean stop” vs “aborted mid-flight”.

Separately (as a belt-and-suspenders measure), we ended up adding a pre-flight gate outside the loop: before each step we check for repeat patterns and enforce a hard budget/loop cap. That way even if abort propagation is imperfect, we still stop runaway loops deterministically.

If anyone’s interested, I’m building ProceedGate around that model (one check before each action; short-lived signed token on allow). Quickstart: https://proceedgate.dev/docs.html.

body:
We hit this in production. Our `generateObject` calls on Bedrock with Claude 4.5/4.6 models are falling back to JSON tool mode despite these models fully supporting native structured output — because we don't enable reasoning for those calls.

Our workaround: We're switching affected call sites to the `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock/anthropic` InvokeModel sub-provider (`createBedrockAnthropic`), which correctly has `supportsNativeStructuredOutput: true`. Then we inject `structuredOutputMode: 'outputFormat'` at the call site since `auto` mode can't resolve Bedrock deployment IDs (ARN-based application inference profiles) via `getModelCapabilities`.

body:
Some _tentative_ decisions on how to move forward with this:

- Implement `uploadFile` (`ai`) and `ProviderFiles.uploadFile` (`@ai-sdk/provider)
- Call the new concept `ProviderReference` instead of `ProviderIndependentID`
- Do not allow use of a string instead of `ProviderReference`
  - It would conflict with the string type in `DataContent`, plus it's unclear whether that was a good idea anyways
  - We can instead offer a `createProviderReference(providerName: string, reference: string)` method
- Include `providerOptions` passthrough, as an escape hatch for provider-specific custom stuff we cannot anticipate
- Keep `uploadFile` light: Return a `ProviderReference`, but don't allow passing in an existing `ProviderReference` to merge into
  - We can instead offer a `mergeProviderReferences` function, keeps functions with a single purpose

These decisions also affect #12855, which should proceed similarly.

body:
Hitting this in production with `ai@6.0.115`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic` latest, using `createAgentUIStreamResponse` + `ToolLoopAgent`.

**Exact UIMessage structure that triggers the bug:**

One assistant UIMessage with two steps (two `step-start` boundaries). Step 1 mixes regular tools with a provider-executed `web_search`:

```
parts:
  step-start                                               ← Step 1
  text (done)
  tool-search_apps  (toolu_01JQy...)  output-available     ← regular tool
  tool-search_apps  (toolu_016Ag...)  output-available     ← regular tool
  tool-web_search   (srvtoolu_01Ep...) output-available    ← providerExecuted
  step-start                                               ← Step 2
  text (done)
  tool-search_apps  (toolu_0173...)   output-available
  tool-get_mcp_status (toolu_01Ea...) output-available
```

**Error:**
```
messages.3: `tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks immediately after: toolu_016Ag..., toolu_01JQy...
```

**Root cause in `convertToModelMessages` (line 202-227):** When processing a step block, `providerExecuted` tool results are inlined into the assistant content (correct). But the `tool-call` entries for regular tools in the same block are also in that assistant content. The Anthropic provider then sees:

```
assistant: [text, tool_use(search_apps), tool_use(search_apps), server_tool_use(web_search), web_search_tool_result]
```

`server_tool_use` + `web_search_tool_result` appear AFTER the regular `tool_use` blocks. Anthropic requires `tool_use` blocks to be the last content items before the `tool_result` user message. The inline web_search result breaks that adjacency.

**Additional note:** The error happens inside the stream body (during API call), not during `createAgentUIStreamResponse` construction. This means `try/catch` around the response creation cannot catch it — the Response object is returned successfully, and the 400 fires when the body is consumed. Any error handling at the caller level is unreachable.

body:
## Confirmed reproduction with `toolSearchBm25_20251119` + Vertex AI Anthropic

We hit this exact bug in production with `toolSearchBm25_20251119` (deferred tool loading) on `@ai-sdk/google-vertex/anthropic` (Vertex AI Claude Sonnet 4.6).

### Setup
- `ai@6.0.153`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic@3.0.68`, `@ai-sdk/google-vertex@4.0.105`
- Platform agent with ~33 tools, 15 marked with `providerOptions: { anthropic: { deferLoading: true } }`
- `anthropic.tools.toolSearchBm25_20251119()` added to the tool set
- Multi-step `streamText()` with `stopWhen: stepCountIs(10)`

### What happens

When the model calls `tool_search_tool_bm25` (server-executed) + a regular tool in the same turn:

**Step 0 → Step 1 transition:** The `prepareStep` callback receives step messages where the assistant message has the `tool-call` for `tool_search` (with `providerExecuted: true`) but the `tool-result` is **completely missing**. The regular tool's `tool-result` is present in the following tool message.

Debug dump from `prepareStep` at step 1:
```json
{
  "stepNumber": 1,
  "toolParts": [
    {"type": "tool-call", "id": "toolu_vrtx_...", "name": "members_get_details", "providerExecuted": false},
    {"type": "tool-call", "id": "srvtoolu_vrtx_...", "name": "anthropic.tool_search_bm25_20251119", "providerExecuted": true},
    {"type": "tool-result", "id": "toolu_vrtx_...", "name": "members_get_details"}
  ]
}
```

The `tool-result` for `srvtoolu_vrtx_...` is gone. The Anthropic API then rejects with:

```
tool_search_tool_bm25 tool use with id srvtoolu_vrtx_... was found without a corresponding tool_search_tool_bm25_tool_result block
```

### Additional finding: content ordering

Even when we work around the missing result by re-injecting from a cache, a second error occurs because the SDK preserves insertion order. The assistant message has `tool_use` (regular) before `server_tool_use` + result. The Anthropic API requires `tool_use` blocks to be **last** in assistant content — `server_tool_use` and its result must come before any regular `tool_use`.

### Workaround (abandoned as too fragile)

We attempted a `prepareStep` workaround that:
1. Cached provider-executed tool results from earlier steps
2. Re-injected missing results into assistant messages
3. Reordered content to put server blocks before regular tool-calls

This partially works but introduces edge cases with the SDK's internal state management. We've **disabled tool search** for now and are waiting for an SDK-level fix.

### Impact

This blocks adoption of `defer_loading` + `toolSearchBm25` for any agent that uses multi-step tool calling (which is most real-world agents). The feature works perfectly in single-step scenarios.
